ITQAN:v4p388/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p388/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p388/r7.claim: The descendant Abraham settled is Ishmael.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from Abraham’s episode and prayer, which asks security for Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, and prosperity for his progeny.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.anchor: the security of Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, prosperity for his progeny

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.claim: Abraham also prayed for forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.anchor: forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.claim: A key theme is the sharp difference between gratitude and ingratitude for God’s blessings.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.anchor: gratitude and ingratitude for God’s Blessings (see vv. 5, 7–8, 28, 32–34, 37)

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r14.claim: Whether people are guided ultimately lies in God’s hands.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r14.anchor: whether they are guided or not is ultimately in God’s Hands (vv. 4, 21, 27, 37)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayers concern Makkah and his children settled there, showing Quraysh that their lives oppose his hopes while Muhammad and his followers fulfill them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The purpose is to make evident to the Quraysh that the whole life that they are leading is totally against the supplications and desires of Abraham (sws).

NAHHAS:v2p370/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p370/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p370/r9.claim: The object is omitted because من indicates it.
NAHHAS:v2p370/r9.anchor: وحذف المفعول لأن من تدل عليه

ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r7.claim: تهوي can mean rising or ascending, from هوي يهوي; تهوى can mean loving, from هوي يهوى. The first reading is preferred.
ZAJJAJ:v3p164/r7.anchor:
فمن قرأ تهوي إليهم فهو على هوى يهوي إذا ارتفع (1)، ومن قرأ
تهوى إليهم فعلى هوي يهوى إذا أحب، والقراءة الأولى هي المختارة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r4.claim: Abraham settled Ishmael and his descendants in barren Mecca by the sacred House, which God had decreed would arise there, so they could establish prayer and worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r4.anchor: بواد غير ذي زرع } مكة حرسها الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:34-37/r5.claim: Abraham asks that people’s hearts yearn to visit the House and that they receive fruits to affirm God’s oneness and glorify Him; the fruit request was discussed in al-Baqara.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham settled his descendants in barren land after leaving a fertile region so they could establish a monotheistic worship center and avoid polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he had settled his progeny in a desolate and barren piece of land after he had migrated from a lush and green region.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sustenance of barren Mecca came from Abraham's supplications, but Quraysh attributed these favors to idols while claiming to follow Abraham.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The sustenance and livelihood found in this barren land are the sole result of Abraham’s (sws) supplications.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، أبو جعفر محمد بن علي، جعفر بن محمد، مجاهد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r3.claim: They read تهوى with fatḥa on the waw, understanding it as love or inclination toward Mecca's people; the standard kasra means to incline toward them, and the variant uses إلى by sense.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r3.anchor: قراءة علي بن أبي طالب وأبي جعفر محمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد -عليهم السلام- ومجاهد: "تهوى"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن عبد الله
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p363/r4.claim: He is reported to read تهوى إليهم; the author explains the standard تهوي as loving and inclining toward them, supported by the Arabic idiom for a camel that settles down.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.claim: For a two-letter noun whose final radical was deleted, nisba may either preserve its form or restore the missing radical; the suffix can prompt restoration as other changes can delete letters.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.anchor: اعلم أن كل اسم على حرفين ذهبت لامه ولم يرد في تثنيته إلى الأصل ولا في ~~الجمع بالتاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.claim: دم and يد allow both دمي/يدي and دموي/يدوي; غدوي is also attested, with poetry and the plural أيد cited to support the underlying forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.anchor: فمن ذلك قولهم في ~~دم دمي وفي يد يدي وإن شئت قلت دموي ويدوي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.claim: He restores the deleted radical in nisba forms such as ثبي/ثبوي and شفي/شفهي; حر allows حري/حرحي, reflecting its deleted final ḥāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.anchor: ومن ذلك أيضا قولهم في ثبة ثبي وثبوي وشفة شفي ~~وشفهي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.claim: For doubled forms such as رب and قرة, restoring the underlying structure avoids retaining an awkward geminate; the same pattern appears in شديدي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىبناتالحرفين)#5.anchor: وإن أضفت إلى رب فيمن خفف فرددت قلت ربي ~~وإنما أسكنت كراهية التضعيف فيعاد بناؤه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.claim: At pause, a preceding quiescent consonant takes the hāʾ's vowel to make the pronoun clearer; Ziyād al-Aʿjam and Abū al-Najm provide poetic examples.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.anchor: ألقوا عليه ~~حركة الهاء حيث حركوا لتبيانها قال الشاعر وهو زياد الأعجم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.speaker: بعض بني تميم من بني عدي
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.claim: Some Banū ʿAdī of Tamīm pronounce قد ضربته and أخذته with kasra to clarify the following hāʾ, not to mark grammatical case; in connected speech the vowel is then followed by wāw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالساكنms760الذيتحركهفيال.anchor: وسمعنا بعض بني تميم من بني عدي يقولون قد ~~ضربته وأخذته كسروا حيث أرادوا أن يحركوها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: A quiescent wāw after kasra becomes yāʾ, as in الميزان and الميعاد; the change eases articulation and parallels avoidance of adjacent wāw and yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.anchor: فمن ذلك قولهم الميزان والميعاد وإنما كرهوا ذلك كما كرهوا الواو مع ~~الياء في ليلة وسيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: After fatḥa, wāw and yāʾ remain in forms such as موعد and موقف; fatḥa and alif are light, and alif requires little tongue or lip articulation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.anchor: فإذا كانتا ساكنتين وقبلهما فتحة مثل موعد ~~وموقف لم تقلب ألفا لخفة الفتحة والألف عليهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: A vocalized wāw is strong enough to remain, as in مود; his comparisons also distinguish it from yāʾ under kasra in ميت.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: Morphological context can preserve wāw in nominal patterns such as توعدة and يوعد, unlike the verb يَعِد; he supports retention with تودية, توسعة, and توصية.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.anchor: وتقول في تفعلة من وعدت ويفعل إذا كان اسمين ولم يكونا من الفعل ~~توعدة ويوعد كما تقول في الموضع والموركة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: A masdar on فعلة deletes wāw like its verb because kasra is heavy with wāw; the pattern is analogized to the verb, while some nouns retain it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.anchor: فأما فعلة إذا كانت مصدرا فإنهم يحذفون الواو منها كما يحذفونها ~~من فعلها لأن الكسر يستثقل في الواو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.claim: The text distinguishes compensatory feminine forms and ordinary nouns, giving وجهة and ولدة/لدة alongside the deletion in جهة and عدة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتقلبفيهالواوياءوذلكإذا.anchor: فإذا لم تكن الهاء فلا حذف لأنه ليس عوض ~~وقد أتموا فقالوا وجهة في جهة وإنما فعلوا ذلك بها مكسورة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r1.claim: A form used as an established noun or adjective is declinable; حطم illustrates the adjective class, with poetic evidence from al-Huṭam al-Qaysī.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r1.anchor: اعلم أن كل فعل كان اسما معروفا في الكلام أو صفة فهو مصروف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r2.claim: These forms decline because they do not resemble augmented verbs, verbs without a nominal counterpart, or forms with a feminine ending.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r2.anchor: الذي في أوله زيادة وليست في آخره زيادة تأنيث

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r3.claim: Umar and Zafar are diptotes because they depart from their original patterns, ʿĀmir and Zāfir; such forms occur as definite names.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r3.anchor: وأما عمر وزفر فإنما منعهم من صرفهما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r4.claim: Sibawayh, following al-Khalil, says Umar declines when indefinite or diminutive because it no longer matches the altered proper-name pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r4.anchor: صرفته لأنه نكرة فتحول عن موضع عامر معرفة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r5.claim: Zuhal is diptote when used as the name of the planet.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r5.anchor: وزحل معدول في حالة إذا أردت اسم الكوكب فلا ينصرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r6.claim: Jamʿ and Kutaʿ are definite forms altered from Jamʿāʾ and Kutaʿāʾ, but they decline when indefinite.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r6.anchor: فقال هما معرفة بمنزلة كلهم وهما معدولتان عن جمع جمعاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r7.claim: Ṣughr as a proper name declines because it resembles Thuquba and is not altered from its expected pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r7.anchor: وسألته عن صغر من قوله الصغري وصغر فقال أصرف هذا في

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r8.claim: Aḫar is diptote in definite and indefinite use because it is an irregular adjective modeled on al-ṭūl, al-wasaṭ, and al-kibar.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r8.anchor: لا ينصرف في معرفة ولا نكرة فقال لأن أخر خالفت أخواتها وأصلها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r9.claim: Vocative forms such as فسق are diptote by analogy with an understood vocative, while a diminutive proper name أخر becomes declinable.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r9.anchor: فلما خالفت الأصل وجاءت صفة بغير الألف واللام تركوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r10.claim: Abu ʿAmr analyzes aḥād, thanā, mathnā, thulāth, and rubāʿ as diptote distributives meaning one by one, two by two, and so on; the Qur'anic phrase and Saʿida's poetry support him.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r11.claim: These distributive forms remain diptote when indefinite because they themselves modify an indefinite noun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r11.anchor: قلت أفتصرفه في النكرة قال لا لأنه نكرة يوصف به نكرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r12.claim: Diminutives of thanā and aḥād decline because diminutive formation removes the altered pattern that caused diptosis.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r12.anchor: ثناء وأحاد صرفته كما صرفت أخيرا وعميرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r13.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r13.claim: Qāl and Qīl as names decline because they are contracted verb forms in the speech of Tamīm, not names coined by alteration like Umar.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r13.anchor: أنك خففت فعل وفعل نفسه كما خففت الحركة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r14.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r14.claim: Umar is not a deletion from ʿĀmir, just as mathnā is not clipped from ithnayn; it is a name built on an altered pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r14.anchor: ولكنه اسم بني من هذا اللفظ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r15.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r15.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r15.claim: A name such as Ḍarb becomes declinable when vowel reduction moves it into a regular declinable noun pattern; this is like diminutive formation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r15.anchor: ثم خففته فأسكنت الراء صرفته لأنك قد أخرجته إلى مثال ما ينصرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r16.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r16.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r16.claim: The shortened name Hār shows why these reduced forms cannot be left diptote merely on the basis of alteration: Hār is clipped from hāʾir.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابفعل)#535/r16.anchor: صرف هذه الأشياء في التخفيف للعدل

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r1.claim: The object of أسكنت may be omitted, yielding ذرية من ذريتي with من ذُرّيتي adjectival; al-Akhfash alternatively treats من as extra.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من ذريتي }: يجوز أن يكون المفعول محذوفا، وهذا الجار صفته

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r2.claim: بواد means في واد, just as one says هو بمكة.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r2.anchor: قوله: " بواد " ، أي: في واد، نحو: هو بمكة.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r3.claim: عند بيتك may describe واد. Abu al-Baqa permits a partitive بدل because the valley is broader than the House’s vicinity; al-Samin objects that عند is noninflecting.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r3.anchor: قوله: { عند بيتك } يجوز أن يكون صفة ل " واد ". وقال أبو البقاء: " ويجوز أن يكون بدلا منه

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r4.claim: The lām in ليقيموا may be imperative or causal; the causal phrase most naturally attaches to أسكنت, or remotely to اجنبني, keeping them from idols so they pray.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r4.anchor: قوله: " ليقيموا " يجوز أن تكون هذه اللام لام أمر، وأن تكون لام علة.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r5.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r5.claim: The common reading أفئدة is plural فؤاد on the pattern غراب/أغربة.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r5.anchor: قوله: { أفئدة من الناس } العامة على " أفئدة " جمع " فؤاد " كغراب وأغربة.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r6.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r6.claim: Hisham from Ibn Amir adds a yāʾ after the hamza, explained as lengthening. Critics object that this is poetic license, while the claim that he merely mistook a softened hamza is dismissed because transmitters are authoritative.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r6.anchor: وقرأ هشام عن ابن عامر بياء بعد الهمزة، فقيل: إشباع، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r7.claim: Poetic examples illustrate lengthening: تريب for ترب and العقراب for العقرب; the second cited line has العقراب.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads إفادة: either a verbal noun from أفاد, meaning people useful to others, or a form originating as وفادة with wāw changed to hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " إفادة " بزنة " رفادة " ، وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون مصدرا لأفاد

SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r9.speaker: أم الهيثم
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r9.claim: Umm al-Haytham reads أفودة with kasra on wāw: either a plural after hamza shifts to wāw following ḍamma, or, in al-Lawāmiʿ, a plural of وفد. Al-Samin notes the expected ordering would be أوفدة and calls the pattern rare.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37/r9.anchor: وقرأت أم الهيثم " أفودة " بواو مكسورة، وفيها وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r1.claim: A long-alif reading آفدة may be metathesis from أفئدة, or active participle of أفد meaning approaching; it may denote a group or groups drawing near.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r1.anchor: وقرىء " آفدة " بزنة ضاربة، وهي تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن تكون مقلوبة من أفئدة

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r2.claim: A shortened reading آفدة may be an active participle on the pattern فرح, or reduced from أفئدة by shifting the hamza vowel and deleting it.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r2.anchor: وقرئ " آفدة " بالقصر، وفيها وجهان أيضا، أحدهما: أن يكون اسم فاعل على فعل كفرح

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes من as marking origin, like القلب مني سقيم for قلبي; the Sheikh objects that no verb here has a starting point from which hearts begin.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن تكون " من " لابتداء الغاية كقولك: " القلب مني سقيم "

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r4.claim: Alternatively من is partitive: without من الناس, the interpretation would have all people make pilgrimage; with it, only some are meant.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنها للتبعيض، وفي التفسير: لو لم يقل " من الناس " لحج الناس كلهم.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r5.claim: تهوي is the second object of جعل. The common kasra reading means hurry or fly eagerly toward them, as in the cited line يهوي مخارمها هوي الأجدل.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r5.anchor: قوله: " تهوي " هذا هو المفعول الثاني للجعل. والعامة " تهوي " بكسر العين بمعنى: تسرع

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r6.claim: The verb normally takes لام, as in a poem about a boy’s hand; here it takes إلى because it carries the sense of تميل, as in a poem about yearning for Mecca.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r7.claim: The cited line تهوي إلى مكة witnesses the verb’s use with إلى to mean yearn or incline.

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r8.speaker: علي وزيد بن علي ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد ومجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r8.claim: These readers give the verb an open wāw: either إلى is extra and it means love them, or the verb carries the sense of تنزع or تميل; the senses have verbal nouns هوي and هوى.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أمير المؤمنين علي وزيد بن علي ومحمد بن علي وجعفر ابن محمد ومجاهد بفتح الواو

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the readings are close in meaning; open-wāw هوى is transitive by itself, with إلى added by analogy to تميل.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " معناهما متقاربان إلا أن هوى - يعني بفتح الواو- متعد بنفسه

SAMIN-DURR:14:37#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#3/r1.speaker: مسلمة بن عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#3/r1.claim: Maslama ibn Abdullah reads تُهوى in the passive, from causative أهوى formed from intransitive هوي, meaning that the hearts are made to hasten toward them.
SAMIN-DURR:14:37#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن عبد الله: " تهوى " بضم التاء وفتح الواو مبنيا للمفعول

ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r1.claim: Abraham says he settled some descendants beside the sanctified Temple in an uncultivable valley so they could devote themselves to prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r1.anchor: Behold, I have settled some of my offspring

ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r2.claim: He asks that people's hearts incline toward his family and that they receive fruitful sustenance, enabling gratitude.
ASAD-NOTES:14:37/r2.anchor: cause Thou, therefore, people's hearts to incline towards them [53] and grant them fruitful sustenance

ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r1.claim: The valley is Mecca's narrow desert valley, enclosed by barren, rocky hills.
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r1.anchor: the narrow desert valley of Mecca, which is enclosed by barren, rocky hills

ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r2.claim: Abraham's offspring here means Ishmael and his descendants, who settled at Mecca.
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n52/r2.anchor: Abraham refers to Ishmael and his descendants who settled at Mecca

ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r1.claim: Asad reads the phrase as people's desire to visit Abraham's family on pilgrimage, thereby helping them live in the holy but barren land.
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r1.anchor: to be desirous of visiting them - namely, on pilgrimage to Mecca - and thus help them to maintain themselves in the holy but barren land

ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r2.speaker: Baghawi, Razi, Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:14:37#n53/r2.claim: Baghawi, Razi, and Ibn Kathir allow the phrase to mean the hearts of some people, understood as believers' hearts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Sincere monotheistic worship can require leaving everything behind, even living alone in a barren land; one must never abandon God and His worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: One thing that is evident from this verse is that for monotheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The House of God is fundamentally a prayer centre, so its true custodians are those who diligently pray rather than claimants who forsake monotheism and prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the House of God is in reality a centre to offer the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Prayer was the House's initial purpose; later it also became a pilgrimage centre and a place for sacrifice commemorating Ishmael's sacrifice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: it also became a centre for ḥajj and also of animal sacrifice to commemorate the sacrifice of Ishmael (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The expression about establishing prayer includes calling people to prayer and arranging for them to perform it, not simply praying.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: included in it is to call people to the prayer and make arrangements for them to offer the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham first prayed that people's hearts incline toward his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: First, he prayed that God inclines

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayer that people's hearts incline toward his descendants soon made the House an attraction for Arabia and, after Muhammad, virtually the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: very soon the House of God became a centre of attraction for all Arabia and after the advent of Muḥammad (sws) of virtually all the world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: For barren Makkah Abraham asked for abundant provisions; it soon became Arabia's trade centre, as discussed at 2:126.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The result of this prayer was that very soon it became the centre of trade in all of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r1.claim: رفث is normally used with ب or مع, but إلى is chosen here because the intended sense is الإفضاء, which takes إلى.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r1.anchor: عداه بإلىوأنت لا تقول: رفثت إلى المرأة، وإنما تقول: رفثت بها أو معها؛

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r2.claim: The phrase يقبل التوبة عن عباده uses عن because repentance is a cause of pardon, as though it said accepts the cause of pardon from His servants.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r2.anchor: لما كانت التوبة سببا للعفو لاحظ معناه فقال: عن عباده،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r3.claim: The author says تهوى إليهم can be transferred from تهوي إليهم or from ʿAlī's reading تهوى; both derivations are possible under his earlier account.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p364/r3.anchor: وأما "تهوى إليهم" فمنقول من تهوي إليهم، وإن شئت كان منقولا من قراءة علي عليه السلام:

NASHR:v2p109/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p109/r1.claim: Both positions are possible, but Egyptian routes make the second, tarqīq when pausing on rāʾ, more apparent for Warsh and explain why sources generalize that rule.
NASHR:v2p109/r1.anchor: والقولان محتملان والثاني أظهر لورش من طرق المصريين، ولذلك أطلقوا ترقيقها

NASHR:v2p109/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p109/r2.claim: When a kasra before rāʾ is the only cause of lightening, pausing removes it: the first view then makes rāʾ heavy, while the second retains lightening because the sukun is incidental.
NASHR:v2p109/r2.anchor: وقد تظهر فائدة الخلاف في الوقف على المكسور إذا لم يكن قبله ما يقتضي الترقيق فإنه بالوقف تزول كسرة الراء الموجبة لترقيقها

NASHR:v2p109/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r3.speaker: مكي
NASHR:v2p109/r3.claim: Makkī says most rules here are analogical and some are transmitted; retaining the connected form at pause, whether with sukun or rawm, has an analogical basis, though he calls the first view better.
NASHR:v2p109/r3.anchor: إنما هو قياس على الأصول وبعضه أخذ سماعا

NASHR:v2p109/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الحصري
NASHR:v2p109/r4.claim: Al-Ḥuṣrī explicitly advocates keeping rāʾ light at pause just as it is in connected recitation when no necessity forces otherwise.

NASHR:v2p109/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن شريح وأبو علي بن بليمة
NASHR:v2p109/r5.claim: Ibn Shurayḥ and Ibn Bulayma reserve tarqīq for Warsh and extend it even to an incidental kasra.
NASHR:v2p109/r5.anchor: أبو عبد الله بن شريح وأبو علي بن بليمة

NASHR:v2p109/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r6.speaker: قوم عن ورش وابن بليمة
NASHR:v2p109/r6.claim: Some transmit tarqīq at pause on examples such as واذكر اسم ربك and فليحذر الذين, but exclude transferred kasra in فليكفر إنا and وانحر إن; Ibn Bulayma also reports tarqīq in both pause and connection, with agreement on lightening in connection.
NASHR:v2p109/r6.anchor: وفليحذر الذين بالترقيق كالوصل واستثنوا فليكفر إنا

NASHR:v2p109/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p109/r7.claim: The author accepts heavy rāʾ during sukun as the stronger position followed in practice, while allowing a distinction between inflectional and structural kasra.
NASHR:v2p109/r7.anchor: أن القول بالتفخيم حالة السكون هو المقبول المنصور

NASHR:v2p109/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p109/r8.claim: After hamzat al-waṣl in a spoken letter-name such as أركما, the two positions yield heavy or light rāʾ and both remain possible because the Arabic pronunciation is not known.
NASHR:v2p109/r8.anchor: فعلى القول بأن أصلها التفخيم تفخم، وعلى القول الآخر ترقق

NASHR:v2p109/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p109/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p109/r9.claim: It is unsupported to claim that rāʾ is inherently heavy simply because it is rāʾ; the defensible claim is that a rāʾ originally bearing fatḥa or ḍamma gains strength for tafkhīm, unless a cause for lightening applies.
NASHR:v2p109/r9.anchor: إن من زعم أن أصل الراء التفخيم إن كان يريد إثبات هذا الوصف للراء مطلقا من حيث إنها راء فلا دليل عليه

NASHR:v2p300/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p300/r7.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p300/r7.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ in إني أسكنت.
NASHR:v2p300/r7.anchor: إني أسكنت فتحها المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v1p15/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r1.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p15/r1.claim: A middle position says using a disputed reading in the obligatory Fātiḥa invalidates prayer when a known alternative is available, because fulfillment of the obligation is uncertain; outside obligatory recitation, invalidation is likewise uncertain.
NASHR:v1p15/r1.anchor: وتوسط بعضهم) فقال: إن قرأ بها في القراءة الواجبة وهي الفاتحة

NASHR:v1p15/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p15/r2.claim: The majority do not require certainty that an unestablished reading is outside the seven aḥruf; the author calls this correct and cites Makkī’s warning against denying it.
NASHR:v1p15/r2.anchor: فالذي عليه الجمهور أنه لا يجب القطع بذلك

NASHR:v1p15/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r3.speaker: بعض أهل الكلام
NASHR:v1p15/r3.claim: Some theologians require certain rejection of any reading not proven among the seven aḥruf; one side faults those who deny the basmala outside al-Naml, while the opposite side faults those who affirm it.
NASHR:v1p15/r3.anchor: وذهب بعض أهل الكلام إلى وجوب القطع بنفيه حتى قطع بعضهم بخطأ

NASHR:v1p15/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p15/r4.claim: The author resolves the dispute by saying the basmala is a Qurʾanic verse in readings that use it to separate sūras, but not in readings that do not separate them with it.
NASHR:v1p15/r4.anchor: والصواب أن كلا من القولين حق، وأنها آية من القرآن في بعض القراءات

NASHR:v1p15/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p15/r5.claim: Declaring anomalous reading forbidden would condemn Companions and Successors who recited it, undermine their transmission of the law, and damage the foundations of Islam.
NASHR:v1p15/r5.anchor: وعلى قول من حرم القراءة بالشاذ يكون عالم من الصحابة وأتباعهم

NASHR:v1p15/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p15/r6.claim: That prohibition would also imply that those who recited anomalous readings never prayed, since a forbidden recitation could not fulfill the obligatory prayer.
NASHR:v1p15/r6.anchor: الذين قرءوا بالشواذ لم يصلوا قط ; لأن تلك القراءة محرمة

NASHR:v1p15/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15/r7.speaker: أبو الفتح محمد بن علي بن دقيق العيد
NASHR:v1p15/r7.claim: Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd finds a difficulty: reports transmitted singly establish that the Prophet recited some anomalous reading, making that reading mutawātir in aggregate despite being called anomalous.
NASHR:v1p15/r7.anchor: وكان مجتهد العصر أبو الفتح محمد بن علي بن دقيق العيد يستشكل الكلام في هذه المسألة

QIRAAT-ER:14:37:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:2#1/r1.claim: The variant has explicit fatḥa on the yāʾ, lengthening the pronoun suffix phonetically without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:2#1/r1.anchor: Variant with explicit fatḥa on yāʾ — phonetic lengthening of the pronoun suffix; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:14:37:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:20#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:20#1/r1.claim: Lvw reads the long-vowel form with yāʾ after hamza; this is a phonological extension with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:14:37:20#1/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: Long vowel variant with yāʾ after hamza — canonical among the Seven; phonological extension without semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the barren valley as Mecca, which had no crops at that time.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بواد غير ذي زرع ﴾ قال مكة لم يكن بها زرع يومئذ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains the hearts’ inclination toward Abraham’s family as hearts yearning toward them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p343#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم ﴾ قال تنزع إليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p442/r2.claim: Hawā means to descend rapidly; the poet's line uses tahwī for swift descent through mountain passes.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.claim: After condemning Quraysh and other Arabs for replacing God's favor with disbelief and idols, the passage recalls their ancestor Abraham: he prayed for Mecca's safety and his descendants' avoidance of idols, then settled them by the House for prayer, contrasting their father's faith with their idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p443/r18.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه تعالى لما ذكر التعجيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r6.claim: Abraham repeats the call to seek an answer and display humility and reliance on God; he uses the plural because the family had just been mentioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r6.anchor: كرر النداء رغبة في الإجابة وإظهارا للتذلل، والالتجاء إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r7.claim: The descendants settled there are Ishmael and his descendants; Hajar was Ishmael’s mother.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r7.anchor: ومن ذريتي هو إسماعيل ومن ولد منه. وذلك هاجر لما ولدت إسماعيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r8.claim: An unattributed report says Abraham travelled with Hajar and the infant on al-Buraq from Syria to Mecca in a day, left them by revelation, and returned that day; their later story is in al-Bukhari and historical accounts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r8.anchor: فروي أنه ركب البراق هو وهاجر والطفل، فجاء في يوم واحد من الشام إلى مكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r9.claim: Min is partitive because Isaac remained in Syria.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r9.anchor: ومن للتبعيض، لأن إسحاق كان في الشام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r10.claim: A valley is the space between two mountains, and it need not contain water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r10.anchor: والوادي ما بين الجبلين، وليس من شرطه أن يكون فيه ماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r11.claim: Abraham knew God would provide water and not abandon Hajar and Ishmael, so he described the valley as lacking cultivation rather than water, its then condition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p445/r11.anchor: وإنما نظر النظر البعيد فقال: غير ذي زرع، ولو لم يعلم ذلك من الله تعالى لقال: غير ذي ماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests that lacking cultivation entails lacking water, since crops cannot grow without water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد يقال إن انتفاء كونه ذا زرع مستلزم لانتفاء الماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the valley as Mecca and explains the phrase as a place where no crop ever grows, like a text with no crookedness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: بواد هو وادي مكة، غير ذي زرع: لا يكون فيه شيء من زرع قط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that قط is used with the past, whereas لا يكون is nonpast; أبدا is the appropriate adverb with a future or present.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r3.anchor: واستعمل قط وهي ظرف لا يستعمل إلا مع الماضي معمولا لقوله: لا يكون، وليس هو ماضيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r4.claim: Mentioning the House as present at the time of the prayer implies it had already been built; the commentary has discussed its building in al-Baqara and Al Imran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: عند بيتك المحرم، يقتضي وجود البيت حالة الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r5.claim: The House is called inviolable because it was kept from the flood, escaped it as an ancient sanctuary, remained protected from tyrants, or is sacred and must not be violated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r5.anchor: ووصف بالمحرم لكونه حرم على الطوفان أي: منع منه، كما سمي بعتيق لأنه أعتق منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r6.claim: The purpose clause attaches to أسكنت, while ربنا is an intervening invocation; the sense is that the honored House should always have worship there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r6.anchor: وليقيموا متعلق بأسكنت. وربنا دعاء معترض، والمعنى: إنه لا يخلو هذا البيت المعظم من العبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r7.claim: Another possibility takes the lām as imperative, making this a prayer that they establish prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r7.anchor: وقيل: هي لام الأمر، دعا لهم بإقامة الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r8.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r8.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi attaches the purpose clause to Abraham’s request to be kept from idol worship; Abu Hayyan calls this very far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الفرج بن الجوزي: اللام متعلقة بقوله: واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام ليقيموا الصلاة انتهى. وهذا بعيد جدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r9.claim: Prayer is singled out either because it is the best act of worship or because it is a cause of every good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r9.anchor: وخص الصلاة دون سائر العبادات لأنها أفضلها، أو لأنها سبب لكل خير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan reads the plural suffix as indicating God had informed Abraham that the child would have descendants there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p446/r10.anchor: وقوله: ليقيموا بضمير الجمع دلالة على أن الله أعلمه بأن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r1.claim: Fuʾād is a heart, named from faʾada, to burn or consume; al-muftaʾad is the fire pit where meat is roasted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r1.anchor: وأفئدة: جمع فؤاد وهي القلوب، سمي القلب فؤاد لإنفاده مأخوذ من فأد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r2.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r2.claim: Muʾarrij says afʾida means groups of people in Quraysh usage; Ibn Bahr adopts this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r2.anchor: وقال مؤرج الأفئدة: القطع من الناس بلغة قريش، وإليه ذهب ابن بحر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r3.claim: Mujahid says that had Abraham asked for the hearts of all people, Persians and Romans would have crowded around the House.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: لو قال إبراهيم عليه السلام: أفئدة الناس، لازدحمت على البيت فارس والروم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Jews and Christians would have made pilgrimage to the House.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: لحجته اليهود والنصارى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r5.claim: The apparent reading makes min partitive: hearts belonging to some people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن من للتبعيض، إذ التقدير: أفئدة من الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows min to indicate origin, construing the phrase as people’s hearts, with an indefinite genitive matching the indefinite أفئدة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن تكون من للابتداء كقولك: القلب مني سقيم يريد قلبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects min as origin because no action here has a starting point and endpoint; partitive min is the apparent construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r7.anchor: ولا يظهر كونها لابتداء الغاية، لأنها ليس لنا فعل يبتدأ فيه لغاية ينتهي إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r8.speaker: هشام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r8.claim: Hisham is reported by al-Hulwani to read أفئدة with a yāʾ after the hamza; some explain this as a report of hamza softening rather than an added yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r8.anchor: وقرأ هشام: أفئدة بياء بعد الهمزة، نص عليه الحلواني عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r9.claim: Al-Dani rejects the claim that Hisham’s and Abu Amr’s transmitters mistook hamza softening for an added letter, since the transmitters knew the readings and their forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمرو والداني الحافظ: ما ذكره صاحب هذا القول لا يعتمد عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r10.claim: The reading آفدة can be an active participle of afada, meaning approached or hurried, or a metathesized plural of fuʾād on the pattern afʿila.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r10.anchor: وقرىء آفدة: على وزن فاعلة، فاحتمل أن يكون اسم فاعل للحذف من أفد أي دنا وقرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r11.claim: The reading أفدة may be a plural of fuʾād with hamza deletion and vowel transfer, though hamza softening is more regular, or an active participle of afada.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r11.anchor: وقرىء أفدة على وزن فعلة، فاحتمل أن يكون جمع فؤاد وذلك بحذف الهمزة ونقل حركتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r12.speaker: أم الهيثم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r12.claim: Umm al-Haytham read أفودة with wāw; al-Lawāmiʿ takes it as a good plural of wafd, though he does not know the woman, while Abu Hatim cites her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r12.anchor: وقرأت أم الهيثم: أفودة بالواو المكسورة بدل الهمزة. قال صاحب اللوامح: وهو جمع وفد، والقراءة حسنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r13.claim: The wāw may replace hamza after a rounded vowel and persist in the plural, or the form may be metathesized from awfud; fuʿl pluralized on afʿila is rare.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p447/r13.anchor: أبدل الهمزة في فؤاد بعد الضمة كما أبدلت في جون، ثم جمع فأقرها في الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r1.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads إفادة on the pattern of ishāra; the hamza appears to replace wāw as in ishāḥ/wishāḥ, yielding “pilgrims,” or the form can mean beneficial people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r1.anchor: علي: إفادة على وزن إشارة. ويظهر أن الهمزة بدل من الواو المكسورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r2.claim: The majority reading تهوي means hurry or fly toward them; because it is imbued with the sense of inclination, it takes إلى although the basic verb takes لام.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تهوي إليهم أي تسرع إليهم وتطير نحوهم شوقا ونزاعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r3.claim: The cited poetry illustrates the majority reading’s sense of hurrying or inclining toward a destination.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r3.anchor: تهوي إلى مكة تبغي الهدى ... ما مؤمن الجن ككفارها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r4.claim: Muslima ibn Abd Allah reads tuhwa as a passive of ahwā, the causative of intransitive hawā: the people are made to hurry toward them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r4.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن عبد الله: تهوى بضم التاء مبنيا للمفعول من أهوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r5.claim: Ali, Zayd ibn Ali, Muhammad ibn Ali, Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, and Mujahid read tahwā from hawā, “love”; with yearning or inclination understood, it takes إلى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب، وزيد بن علي، ومحمد بن علي، وجعفر بن محمد، ومجاهد: تهوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r6.claim: Since the valley has no fruit, God supplies it by bringing fruit from other lands, as another verse describes produce being brought to the sanctuary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r6.anchor: وارزقهم من الثمرات مع سكانهم واديا ما فيه شيء منها بأن يجلب إليهم من البلاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r7.speaker: مسلم بن محمد الطائفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r7.claim: A report from Muslim ibn Muhammad al-Taifi says Gabriel carried a piece of Palestine—or, in another version, Jordan—around the House seven times; it became Taif, a place of Thaqif with trees and fruit. A similar report is attributed to Ibn Abbas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r7.anchor: وروي عن مسلم بن محمد الطائفي أنه لما دعا عليه السلام بأن يرزق سكان مكة الثمرات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God answered by making Mecca a secure sanctuary supplied with every kind of fruit, surpassing fertile regions in its abundance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري النعمة في أن يرزقوا أنواع الثمرات حاضرة في واد بباب ليس فيه نجم ولا شجر ولا ماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari marvels that fruits from different seasons—spring, summer, and autumn—can appear together in one day in this barren valley.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448/r9.anchor: اجتماع البواكير والفواكه المختلفة الأزمان من الربيعية والصيفية والخريفية في يوم واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers that the townhood request is retold in 14:37 as hearts inclining to Abraham's family for residence, as Ibn ʿAbbās explains, not merely pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r5.anchor: إذ المسؤول هويها إليهم المساكنة كما روى عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative is an aside reinforcing the preceding call to gratitude through faith and good works and warning against their opposites; it gently invites the Meccan rejecters.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r7.anchor: واردة على سبيل الاعتراض مقررة لما حث عليه من الشكر بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.claim: Irshād says the passage heightens the Prophet's astonishment: Quraysh denied special and general blessings, disobeyed Abraham, and replaced the sacred city with ruin despite God's answered prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p233/r8.anchor: وفي إرشاد العقل السليم أن المراد منها تأكيد ماسلف من تعجيبه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r1.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r1.claim: Al-Baḥr says the repeated address seeks an answer and refuge in God, and the plural pronoun reflects Abraham's mention of his sons in the prior verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r1.anchor: قال في البحر كرر النداء رغبة في الإجابة والالتجاء إليه تعالى وأتى بضمير الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects that explanation because it would also predict a plural address in 14:36; the plural here instead suits the descendants who are the subject of the settlement and its preparatory prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r2.anchor: وتعقب بأن ذلك يقتضي ضمير الجماعة في ( رب إنهن ) الخ مع أنه جيء فيه بضمير الواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r3.claim: Min may be partitive, with the phrase functioning as the object by interpretation, or the object may be omitted and the phrase serve as its adjective; min may then be partitive or explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r3.anchor: بمعنى بعض وهي في تأويل المفعول به أي أسكنت بعض ذريتي

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r4.claim: Some call min extra following al-Akhfash, but al-Ālūsī dismisses that analysis as unacceptable to sound judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r4.anchor: زائدة على مذهب الأخفش لايرتضيه سليم البصيرة كما لايخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r5.claim: The settled descendant is Ishmael and the descendants he would have; settling him peacefully entails settling them, while the explicit plural purpose clause motivates the broader reference.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r5.anchor: والمراد بالمسكن إسماعيل عليه السلام ومن سيولد له

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r6.claim: Settlement applies literally to Ishmael and figuratively to his offspring; interpreters who disallow combining literal and figurative senses must posit a general metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236/r6.anchor: الاسكان له حقيقة ولأولاده مجاز فمن لم يجوز الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī recounts that Hagar, an Egyptian Copt given to Abraham by Sarah, bore Ishmael; after Sarah became jealous, Abraham took mother and child to the empty, waterless Meccan valley with dates and water.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن هاجر أم إسماعيل كانت أمه من القبط لسارة فوهبتها من إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r2.claim: Hagar repeatedly asked why Abraham was leaving them in a deserted valley; when she learned God had commanded it, she trusted that He would not abandon them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r2.anchor: الله أمرك بهذا قال : نعم ( 1 ) قالت : إذن لايضيعنا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r3.claim: Abraham left until hidden from them, turned toward the House, then prayed the words of this verse with raised hands; the House then stood on a rise where floodwaters passed to either side.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r3.anchor: استقبل بوجهه البيت وكان إذ ذاك مرتفعا من الأرض كالرابية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r4.claim: When their water ran out, Hagar's thirsty infant writhed; she ran between Ṣafā and Marwa seven times searching for help, which the account gives as the origin of the seven circuits of saʿy.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r4.anchor: ففعلت ذلك سبع مرات ولذلك سعى الناس بينهما سبعا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r5.claim: An angel dug with his heel at Zamzam until water appeared; Hagar drank and nursed Ishmael while the spring flowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r5.anchor: فإذا هي بالملك عند موضع زمزم فبحث بعقبه حتى ظهر الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r6.claim: The angel reassured Hagar that God would not abandon them and that the boy and his father would build God's House there; later a Jurhum party found the water, settled with her by exchanging milk for access, and married Ishmael to one of their women.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r6.anchor: لاتخافي الضيعة فان ههنا بيت الله تعالى يبنيه هذا الغلام وأبوه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r7.claim: The valley is Mecca; “not possessing cultivation” intensifies “uncultivated,” meaning it was unfit for farming, as in the phrase “an Arabic Qur'an with no crookedness.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r7.anchor: ووصفه بذلك دون غير مزروع للمبالغة لأن المعنى ليس صالحا للزرع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r8.claim: The wording is compared with Qur'an 39:28, “an Arabic Qur'an with no crookedness,” where the construction likewise intensifies the negation.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج ) وكان

ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains that Abraham omitted “without water” because he knew God would provide water for Ishmael and Hagar and would not neglect them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p236#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وإنما لم يصفه عليه السلام بالخلو عن الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān argues that saying the valley had no crops already entails that it had no water, since crops cannot exist without water.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حيان بعد نقله وقد يقال : إن انتفاء كونه ذا زرع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r2.claim: Some say water was not Abraham's chief concern because floodwater could be stored; he chiefly sought fruit, and the description emphasizes the family's complete dependence on God's provision.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes “at Your inviolable House” as an adverbial phrase modifying “I settled”; Abū al-Baqā instead calls it an adjective of “valley” or an apposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r3.anchor: ظرف لأسكنت كقولك : صليت بمكة عند الركن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqā analyzes the phrase as an adjective of “valley” or as an apposition; al-Ālūsī prefers the adverbial attachment because it highlights settlement beside God's sanctuary.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r4.anchor: وزعم أبو البقاء أنه صفة ( واد ) أو بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r5.claim: The House is called inviolable because God forbade violating or slighting it; alternatively, it has always been protected and feared by tyrants, or the flood was prevented from overtaking it, hence its name al-ʿAtīq.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r5.anchor: معنى كون البيت محرما أن الله تعالى حرم التعرض له والتهاون به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the explanation that it is called inviolable because visitors forbid themselves otherwise lawful acts; Abraham calls it a House in reference either to its former state or to its future construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r6.anchor: وأبعد من قال إنه سمي محرما لأن الزائرين يحرمون على أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r7.claim: The lām is purposive, with an implicit أن making the verb subjunctive, and the phrase attaches to “I settled”; repeating “Our Lord” emphasizes establishing prayer, the pillar of religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r7.anchor: لأن يقيموا فللام جارة والفعل منصوب بأن مضمرة بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r8.claim: The barren valley and sacred House imply that Abraham settled them there for worship alone: establishing prayer, cultivating the sanctuary through remembrance and worship, and seeking God's mercy and nearness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r8.anchor: ما أسكنتهم بهذا الوادي البلقع الخالي من كل مرتفق ومرتزق

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r9.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r9.claim: Mālik holds that a purpose clause implies exclusivity and uses “that you may ride them” in 16:8 to argue that the animals are not for eating.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r9.anchor: وعن مالك أن التعليل يفيد الحصر فقد استدل بقوله تعالى : ( لتركبوها )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r10.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r10.claim: Kashf derives the exclusivity from an implied later verb, “I settled them in this settlement so that they would establish prayer”; the intervening second “Our Lord” shows the phrase does not modify the stated verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r10.anchor: وفي الكشف أن استفادة الحصر من تقدير محذوف مؤخر يتعلق به الجار والمجرور

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers deriving exclusivity from the sequence: barren land rules out farming, the House establishes worship, and the purpose clause identifies prayer; the repeated address is parenthetical emphasis, so no omitted verb is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r11.anchor: واختار بعضهم ماذكرناه أولا في وجه الاستفادة وقال : انه معنى لطيف

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r12.claim: A less plausible reading treats the lām as an imperative asking God to enable them to pray; Ibn al-Jawzī's still more remote proposal attaches it to “keep me and my sons away from idolatry.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r12.anchor: وقيل : اللام لام الأمر والفعل مجزوم بها والمراد هو الدعاء لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r13.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r13.claim: The plural “they may establish” indicates that God informed Abraham that Ishmael would have descendants in that place.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r13.anchor: وفي قوله : ( ليقيموا ) بضمير الجمع على مافي البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r14.claim: “Hearts from among people” means some hearts, so the request does not entail that all nations crowd the family; the author assumes the prayer was answered and the generic plural can denote everyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r14.anchor: أي أفئدة من أفئدتهم ( تهوي إليهم ( أي تسرع إليهم شوقا وودادا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r15.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r15.claim: Ibn Jubayr says that if Abraham had asked for the hearts of all people, Jews and Christians would have made pilgrimage to the House.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p237/r15.anchor: وروى عن ابن جبير أنه قال : لو قال عليه السلام : أفئدة الناس لحجت البيت اليهود والنصارى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Ibn Jubayr's reading is not apt if Abraham asked for hearts to incline to the family for residence rather than to the House for pilgrimage; the two readings can nevertheless coexist.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r1.anchor: وتعقب بأنه غير مناسب للمقام إذا المسؤول توجيه القلوب إليهم للمساكنة معهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r2.speaker: عكرمة وطاوس وعطاء بن أبي رباح
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r2.claim: Al-Ḥakam says he asked ʿIkrima, Ṭāwūs, and ʿAṭāʾ about the phrase; they answered that hearts incline to the House and people come to it, glossing this as love of Mecca for pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r2.anchor: عن الحكم قال : سألت عكرمة وطاوسا وعطاء ابن أبي رباح عن هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r3.claim: Some interpret the request as directing hearts to the House; although this differs from the apparent reference to Abraham's family, the pilgrimage reading need not conflict with a request for people to settle with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r3.anchor: على أن بعضهم جعل هذا دعاء بتوجيه القلوب إلى البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān doubts that min marks a point of origin, since there is no verb here from which hearts could begin toward an endpoint.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r4.anchor: واعترضه أبو حيان بأنه لايظهر كونها للابتداء لأنه لافعل هنا يبتدأ فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r5.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r5.claim: A senior scholar replies that the verb “incline” supplies the motion: hearts begin their inclination from people toward the family, as indicated by “to them.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r5.anchor: وتعقبه بعض الاجلة بقوله : وفيه بحث فان فعل الهوى للأفئدة يبتدأ به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r6.speaker: مولانا الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r6.claim: Al-Shihāb favors min of origin: partitivity adds no information because everyone knows a person's heart is part of them; the phrase instead depicts inclination as arising from the whole person.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r6.anchor: وذكر مولانا الشهاب في توجيه الابتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r7.claim: The phrase “my bones are weak from me” in 19:4 illustrates the point that min of origin can identify the source of an attribute without stating a meaningful partitive fact.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r7.anchor: وقد قيل : إن جميع معاني ( من ) دائرة على الابتداء والتبعيض هنا لايظهر فيه فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r8.claim: Afʾida is the first object of “make” and the plural of fuʾād; lexicographers gloss it as the heart, called fuʾād when its burning or glowing quality is considered.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p238/r8.anchor: والأفئدة مفعول أول لاجعل وهو جمع فؤاد وفسروه على مافي البحر وغيره بالقلب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that faʾīd meat means roasted meat, clarifying the word-family used in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r1.anchor: فأدت اللحم أي شويته ولحم فئيد أي مشوي

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r2.speaker: ابن بحر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r2.claim: Ibn Baḥr takes afʾida as groups of people in Quraysh usage, rather than hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r2.anchor: وقيل : الأفئدة هنا القطع من الناس بلغة قريش واليه ذهب ابن بحر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r3.claim: On Ibn Baḥr’s reading, the clause tahwī is the second object of afʾida.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r4.claim: Hawā originally means to drop rapidly, and the verb would normally take lām; here ilā reflects an included sense of inclination, as the cited verses of poetry illustrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r4.anchor: وأصل الهوى الهبوط بسرعة وفي كلام بعضهم السرعة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r5.claim: The fa in fajʿal marks the request as following from the preceding circumstances, which were beginnings of an answer to Abraham’s prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r5.anchor: ولما كان ماتقدم كالمبادي لأجابة دعائه عليه السلام واعطاء مسؤوله جاء بالفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r6.speaker: هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r6.claim: Hishām read afʾida with an additional yāʾ after the hamza; al-Ḥulwānī explicitly transmitted this from him.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r6.anchor: وقرأ هشام ( أفئيدة ) بياء بعد الهمزة نص عليه الحلواني عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r7.speaker: قالوا
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r7.claim: Some explain Hishām’s form as a hamza softened toward yāʾ, with a transmitter’s phrasing mistaken for a yāʾ after the hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r7.anchor: قالوا : إن هشاما قرأ بتسهيل الهمزة كالياء فعبر عنها الراوي بالياء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r8.speaker: الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r8.claim: Al-Dānī rejects the claim of a transmitter’s misunderstanding: Hishām’s transmitters were too expert in readings and their forms for that mistake.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r8.anchor: تعقب ذلك الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني بأن النقلة عن هشام كانوا من أعلم الناس بالقراءة ووجوهها

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r9.claim: The reading āfida has two derivations: metathesis and hamza change in a plural pattern, or the participle of afida, meaning to draw near or hurry, describing a group.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r9.anchor: وقريء ( آفدة ) على وزن ضاربة وفيه احتمالان أحدهما أن يكون قدمت فيه الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r10.claim: Afida without lengthening can mean an eager or hastening group, or derive from afʾida by transferring the hamza’s vowel and deleting it, a recognized analysis among morphologists and readers.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r10.anchor: وقريء ( أفدة ) بفتح الهمزة من غير مد وكسر الفاء بعدها دال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r11.speaker: الاولون وصاحب النشر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r11.claim: Earlier authorities allow retaining a hamza after a sound consonant with sukūn or transferring its vowel and deleting it, but not between-between; the later authority al-Nashr records that latter option as very weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r11.anchor: اذا تحركت الهمزة بعد ساكن صحيح تبقى أو تنقل حركتها إلى ماقبلها وتحذف ولايجوز جعلها بين بين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r12.speaker: أم الهيثم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r12.claim: Umm al-Haytham read afūda with wāw instead of hamza; al-Lawāmiḥ calls it a good reading and parses it as the plural of wafd, while noting he did not know her.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r12.anchor: وقرأت أم الهيثم ( أفودة ) بالواو المكسورة بدل الهمزة قال صاحب اللوامح : وهو جمع وفد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r13.claim: Abū Ḥayyān suggests afūda may preserve wāw substituted for hamza in fuʾād, or may be plural wafd; the latter has the irregular plural pattern afʿila.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r13.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : يحتمل أنه أبدل الهمزة في فؤاد ثم جمع وأقرت الواو في الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r14.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r14.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī read ifāda; its hamza may replace a wāw as in wišāḥ/ʾišāḥ, yielding ifāda for those who come, or mean people who benefit others.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r14.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( افادة ) على وزن امارة ويظهر أن الهمزة بدل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r15.speaker: مسلمة بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r15.claim: Muslima b. ʿAbd Allāh read tahwā passively, from causative ahwā, meaning that the hearts are made to hurry toward them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r15.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن عبدالله ( تهوى ) بضم التاء مبنيا للمفعول من أهوى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r16.speaker: علي ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r16.claim: ʿAlī, members of his household, and Mujāhid read tahwā as the present of hawiya, ‘to love’; ilā is used in the preceding sense of inclination.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r16.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وجماعة من أهله ومجاهد ( تهوى ) مضارع هو بمعنى أحب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r17.claim: The requested provision is for Abraham’s descendants settled there, and may also include the people who join them; some say specifying believers was unnecessary after the prayer for prayer’s establishment, unlike 2:126.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r17.anchor: أي ذريتي الذين أسكنتهم هناك وجوز أن يريدهم والذين ينحازون اليهم من الناس وإنما لم يخص عليه السلام الدعاء بالمؤمنين منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r18.claim: God can supply fruits by creating nearby settlements or importing produce from distant regions; both happened, so Mecca had fruits from different seasons together.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r18.anchor: بأن تجعل بقربهم قرى يحصل فيها ذلك أو تجبى اليهم من الاقطار الشاسعة وقد حصل كلا الامرين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r19.speaker: محمد بن مسلم الطائفي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r19.claim: A report collected by al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim says Ṭāʾif was in Palestine and God moved it to its present place as provision for the sanctuary after Abraham’s prayer; another version has Gabriel carry it around the House seven times, explaining its name, then set it near Mecca.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r19.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن محمد بن مسلم الطائفي أن الطائف كانت من أرض فلسطين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to have related a similar account of Ṭāʾif being moved in response to Abraham’s supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r20.anchor: وروى نحو ذلك عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r21.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r21.claim: Al-Zuhrī reports that God moved a Syrian village and placed it at Ṭāʾif in response to Abraham’s prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r21.anchor: عن الزهري أن الله تعالى نقل قرية من قرى الشام فوضعها بالطائف

ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r22.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts the reports’ reliability and says Abraham apparently sought provision, not the transfer of fertile land, since provision needs no transfer; he nevertheless affirms God’s power to do whatever He wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p239/r22.anchor: والظاهر أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لم يكن مقصوده من هذا الدعاء نقل أرض منبتة من فلسطين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r1.claim: The intended gratitude is shown by establishing prayer and performing the other rites of servitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r1.anchor: تلك النعمة باقامة الصلاة واداء سائر مراسم العبودية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r2.claim: The passage supports the principle that worldly benefits are sought as a means of performing worship and acts of obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r2.anchor: على أن تحصيل منافع الدنيا إنما هي ليستعان بها على اداء العبادات واقامة الطاعات

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r3.claim: Abraham’s appeal observes exemplary humility and proper supplicatory etiquette in presenting need and seeking mercy; God accepted it and granted the request.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240/r3.anchor: ولا يخفى مافي دعائه عليه السلام من مراعاة حسن الأدب والمحافظة على قوانين الضراعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r1.claim: The preposition min is partitive; the sense is that Abraham settled one child from among his descendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r1.anchor: أدخل "من" للتبعيض، ومجاز الآية: أسكنت من ذريتي ولدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r2.claim: The barren valley is Mecca, a valley between two mountains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r2.anchor: {بواد غير ذي زرع} وهو مكة؛ لأن مكة واد بين جبلين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r3.claim: The House is called muḥarram because acts forbidden there are permitted elsewhere.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r3.anchor: {عند بيتك المحرم} سماه محرما لأنه يحرم عنده ما لا يحرم عند غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Hājar first made a waist wrapper to conceal her tracks from Sarah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أول ما اتخذ النساء المنطق من قبل أم إسماعيل، اتخذت منطقا لتعفي أثرها على سارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts Abraham bringing the nursing Hājar and infant Ishmael to a tree above Zamzam, when Mecca had no inhabitants or water, and leaving dates and a waterskin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r5.anchor: ثم جاء بها إبراهيم عليه السلام، وبابنها إسماعيل، وهي ترضعه، حتى وضعهما عند البيت عند دوحة فوق زمزم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r6.claim: Hājar followed Abraham and repeatedly asked why he left them in an empty valley; when she asked if God had commanded it, he said yes, and she trusted God would not abandon them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r6.anchor: فقالت له: آلله أمرك بهذا؟ قال: نعم، قالت: إذن لا يضيعنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r7.claim: Once beyond sight at the mountain pass, Abraham faced the House, raised his hands, and prayed with the words of this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r7.anchor: حتى إذا كان عند الثنية حيث لا يرونه استقبل بوجهه البيت، ثم دعا بهؤلاء الدعوات فرفع يديه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r8.claim: After the water in the skin ran out, Hājar and Ishmael became thirsty; she saw him writhing and went away because she could not bear to watch.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r8.anchor: حتى إذا نفد ما في السقاء عطشت وعطش ابنها، وجعلت تنظر إليه يتلبط أو قال يتلوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
