BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r9.claim: Hājar climbed al-Ṣafā, the nearest mountain, and looked across the valley for anyone, but saw no one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r9.anchor: فوجدت الصفا أقرب جبل في الأرض يليها، فقامت عليه ثم استقبلت الوادي تنظر هل ترى أحدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r10.claim: She descended into the valley, ran with great effort to al-Marwa, climbed it, and looked for someone but saw no one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r10.anchor: فهبطت من الصفا حتى إذا بلغت الوادي رفعت طرف درعها، ثم سعت سعي الإنسان المجهود حتى جاوزت الوادي، ثم أتت المروة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p355/r11.claim: Hājar repeated the journey between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa seven times.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r1.claim: Al-afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, meaning hearts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r1.anchor: الأفئدة: جمع الفؤاد {تهوي إليهم} تشتاق وتحن إليهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r2.claim: The hearts long for and yearn toward them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r3.claim: Al-Suddī asks God to incline people's hearts toward this place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r3.anchor: قال السدي: معناه أمل قلوبهم إلى هذا الموضع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r4.claim: Mujāhid says a request for all people's hearts would draw Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians to crowd them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد: لو قال أفئدة الناس لزاحمتكم فارس والروم والترك والهند

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jews, Christians, and Magians would have made pilgrimage, but the wording limits the request to Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لحجت اليهود والنصارى والمجوس، ولكنه قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r6.claim: He asks for fruit like that given to inhabitants of well-watered towns, so his family may give thanks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357/r6.anchor: {وارزقهم من الثمرات} ما رزقت سكان القرى ذوات الماء، {لعلهم يشكرون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r5.claim: Min means some descendants or descendants of descendants; the object is omitted and means Ishmael and his line, whose settlement is implied by settling him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r5.anchor: { ربنا إنى أسكنت من ذريتى } أي بعض ذريتي أو ذرية من ذريتي فحذف المفعول وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r6.claim: The barren valley is rocky Mecca, which does not grow crops.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r6.anchor: { بواد غير ذى زرع } يعني وادي مكة فإنها حجرية لا تنبت.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r7.claim: The House is forbidden to violate or neglect, or has always been revered and feared by tyrants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r7.anchor: { عند بيتك المحرم } الذي حرمت التعرض له والتهاون به، أو لم يزل معظما ممنعا يهابه الجبابرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r8.claim: Alternatively, the Flood was kept from overtaking the House, hence its name ʿatīq, freed from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r8.anchor: أو منع منه الطوفان فلم يستول عليه ولذلك سمي عتيقا أي أعتق منه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r9.claim: If Abraham prayed before arriving, the wording may refer to what had been or to what would later come to be.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r9.anchor: ولو دعا بهذا الدعاء أول ما قدم فلعله قال ذلك باعتبار ما كان أو ما سيؤول إليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r10.speaker: رُوي
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r10.claim: A report says Sarah gave Hajar to Abraham; after Hajar bore Ishmael and Sarah became jealous, Abraham settled them at Mecca, Zamzam appeared, Jurhum found them by following birds, exchanged milk for water, and Hajar agreed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r10.anchor: روي أن هاجر كانت لسارة رضي الله عنها فوهبتها لإبراهيم عليه السلام فولدت منه إسماعيل عليه السلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r11.claim: The lām is purposive and attaches to settled: Abraham settled them in the barren valley solely so they could establish prayer at the House.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r11.anchor: اللام لام كي وهي متعلقة ب { أسكنت } أي ما أسكنتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r12.claim: Repeating the address shows prayer is the primary purpose of settling them; the prayer asks God to grant them success in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r12.anchor: وتكرير النداء وتوسيطه للاشعار بأنها المقصودة بالذات من إسكانهم ثمة، والمقصود من الدعاء توفيقهم لها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r13.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r13.claim: Alternatively, the lām is imperative: Abraham asks God to enable them to pray.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r13.anchor: وقيل لام الأمر والمراد هو الدعاء لهم بإقامة الصلاة كأنه طلب منهم الإقامة

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r14.claim: Min is partitive: some human hearts; it is said asking for all hearts would have brought crowds of Persians and Romans and pilgrims among Jews and Christians.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r14.anchor: و { من } للتبعيض ولذلك قيل لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليهم فارس والروم ولحجت اليهود والنصارى

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r15.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r15.claim: Alternatively, min marks origin, as in saying the heart is from me: hearts belonging to people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r15.anchor: أو للابتداء كقولك: القلب مني سقيم أي أفئدة ناس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r16.speaker: هشام
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r16.claim: Hisham, with a reported qualification, reads afʾīdah with an added yāʾ after the hamza.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r17.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r17.claim: A variant āfidah may be metathesized from afʾidah or mean groups that hasten toward the family.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r17.anchor: اسم فاعل من أفدت الرحلة إذا عجلت أي جماعة يعجلون نحوهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r18.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r18.claim: Another variant drops the hamza for ease and may derive from afada.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r18.anchor: وإن كان الوجه فيه إخراجهما بين ويجوز أن يكون من أفد

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r19.claim: The hearts hasten toward them with longing and affection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r19.anchor: { تهوى إليهم } تسرع إليهم شوقا وودادا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r20.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r20.claim: A passive reading means someone else inclines hearts toward them; another derives from hawiya, to love, made transitive by yearning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r20.anchor: وقرىء { تهوى } على البناء للمفعول من أهوى إليه غيره و { تهوى } من هوى يهوي إذا أحب

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r21.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r21.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r21.claim: Despite the barren valley, God answered by making it a secure sanctuary supplied with fruits of every kind, even fruits of every season on one day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:36-37/r21.anchor: فأجاب الله عز وجل دعوته فجعله حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء حتى توجد فيه الفواكه الربيعية والصيفية والخريفية في يوم واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r8.claim: After asking protection from harms caused by humans and Satan through the city's security and faith, Ibrāhīm states why he chose this place and seeks benefits for its inhabitants.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r8.anchor: ولما دعا بدرء المفاسد الناشئة من من نوعي الإنسان والشيطان بأمن البلد وإيمانه ذكر السبب الحامل له

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r9.claim: Al-Biqāʿī conjectures that God had told Ibrāhīm, after announcing Isaac, that his descendants would multiply like stars; he stresses “some of my progeny” because the request seems extraordinary and expresses his desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r9.anchor: وكأن الله سبحانه كان قد أخبره أنه يكثر نسله حتى يمونوا كالنجوم , وذلك بعد البشارو بإسحاق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r10.claim: The valley is Mecca, a low open space among mountains through which torrents run.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r10.anchor: هو مكة المشرفة لكونها في فضاء منخفض بين جبال تجري به السيول

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r11.claim: Having denied them worldly provision from crops, the prayer turns to otherworldly benefit, since the two abodes are rivals that do not combine.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r11.anchor: ولما نفي الرفد الدنيوي , أثبت له الأخروي , إشارة إلى أن الدارين ضرتان لا تجتمعان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r12.claim: Al-Biqāʿī thinks the prayer may have followed construction of the House; it is sacrosanct because God forbade trespass, made it awe-inspiring, and established a sanctuary for wild animals and birds.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r12.anchor: الذي حرمت التعرض إليه ومنعته بالهيبة فلم يملكه أحد سواك , وجعل له حريم يأمن فيه الوحش والطير

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r13.claim: Suknā is taking a dwelling to reside in when one wishes; a wādī is a mountain's slope, hence rivers are called valleys because their banks resemble mountains; zarʿ is spreading, stemless vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r13.anchor: والكسنى : اتخاذ مأوى يسكن إليه متى شاء , والوادي : سفح الجبل العظيم , ومنه قيل للأنهار : أودية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r14.claim: He settled them there for prayer alone, which is incompatible with worshipping anyone else; those present at the House are especially entitled to establish prayer directed toward it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r14.anchor: ما أسكنتهم في هذا الوادي الموصوف إلا لهذا الغرض المنافي لعبادة غيرك , ولأن أولى الناس بإقامتها حاضرو البيت

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r15.claim: Hearts are hearts burning with longing; among people susceptible to agitation, that yearning keeps them from restlessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r15.anchor: قلوبا محترقة بالأشواق { من الناس } أي من أفئدة الذين هم أهل للاضطراب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r16.claim: Tahwī means to head toward them and hurry with desire and longing like someone descending from a height; “toward them” clarifies the destination and intensifies the image through distance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r16.anchor: أي تقصدهم فتسرع نحوهم برغبة وشوق إسراع من ينزل من حالق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r17.claim: He asks that visitors drawn to them bring them fruits grown in their land, thus providing sustenance to them and their neighbors.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r17.anchor: على يد من يهوي إليهم { من الثمرات } أي التي أنبتها في بلادهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r18.claim: Their hoped-for gratitude follows extraordinary provision in a place lacking crops by God's care, so they can worship Him; God answered the prayer, and the verse reminds Quraysh of blessings through their forefather Ibrāhīm, who forbade idols.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p190/r18.anchor: وقد أجاب الله دعوته ؛ فالآية لتذكير قريش بهذه النعم الجليلة عليهم ببركة أبيهم الأعظم

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r5.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r5.claim: Saʿd’s report says Sarah, long childless, gave Abraham Hajar; after Ishmael’s birth Sarah became jealous and swore to cut three parts from her.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r5.anchor: من طريق عامر بن سعد عن أبيه قال: كانت سارة عليها السلام تحت إبراهيم عليه السلام فمكثت معه دهرا لا ترزق منه ولدا

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r6.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r6.claim: Abraham proposed piercing Hajar’s ears and circumcising her to satisfy Sarah’s oath; the earrings made Hajar more beautiful.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r6.anchor: فقال لها إبراهيم عليه السلام: هل لك أن تبري يمينك فقالت: كيف أصنع قال: اثقبي أذنيها واخفضيها والخفض هو الختان

DURR-FULL:v5p46/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r7.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r7.claim: The report says Abraham moved Hajar to Mecca and visited daily from Syria on al-Buraq because he could scarcely bear separation.
DURR-FULL:v5p46/r7.anchor: ووجد بها إبراهيم عليه السلام وجدا شديدا فنقلها إلى مكة فكان يزورها في كل يوم من الشام على البراق

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the descendants settled in Mecca as Ishmael and his mother.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع} قال: اسكن إسماعيل وأمه مكة

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says specifying some people prevented Turks and Romans from overwhelming the sanctuary; asking for all people would have drawn them.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} لو قال: فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r3.claim: Mujahid likewise says that asking for all people’s hearts would have crowded Mecca with Persians and Romans.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} قال: لو قال أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r4.speaker: عكرمة وطاوس وعطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r4.claim: ʿIkrima, Tawus, and ʿAta say hearts incline to the House and its visitors come; another wording says people long to go to Mecca for pilgrimage.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r4.anchor: عن الحكم قال: سألت عكرمة وطاوسا وعطاء بن أبي رباح عن هذه الآية فقالوا: البيت تهوي إليه قلوبهم يأتونه

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r5.claim: Qatada glosses tahwī as being drawn toward them.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} قال: تنزع إليهم

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r6.speaker: محمد بن مسلم الطائفي
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Taʾifi says God moved al-Taif from Palestine after Abraham prayed for fruit for the sanctuary.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم الطائفي أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما دعا للحرم وارزق أهله من الثمرات نقل الله الطائف من فلسطين

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r7.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri says God transferred a Syrian village to Taif in response to Abraham’s prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r7.anchor: عن الزهري رضي الله عنه قال: إن الله تعالى نقل قرية من قرى الشام فوضعها بالطائف لدعوة إبراهيم عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r8.claim: Qatada identifies the uncultivated valley as Mecca, where there was no agriculture then.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r8.anchor: عن قتادة {بواد غير ذي زرع} قال: مكة لم يكن بها زرع يومئذ

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r9.claim: Qatada says God purified the Sacred House from evil, made it a sanctuary and prayer direction, and Abraham chose it for his son.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم} وأنه بيت طهره الله من السوء وجعله قبلة

DURR-FULL:v5p47/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r10.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r10.claim: ʿUmar says Tasm and then Jurhum violated the sanctuary and were destroyed; he warns Quraysh against repeating their conduct.
DURR-FULL:v5p47/r10.anchor: ذكر لنا أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال في خطبته: إن هذا البيت أول من وليه ناس من (طسم) فعصوا فيه واستخفوا بحقه

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r1.claim: In the continuation of ʿUmar’s speech, he warns Quraysh not to violate the sanctuary; prayer there is worth a hundred elsewhere, and sins likewise carry added weight.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r1.anchor: فلا تعصوا ولا تستخفوا بحقه ولا تستحلوا حرمته وصلاة فيه أفضل من مائة صلاة بغيره والمعاصي فيه على قدر ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham asked God to make some people desire to settle in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} قال: إن إبراهيم سأل الله أن يجعل أناسا من الناس يهوون سكنى مكة

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r3.claim: Al-Suddi explains that hearts are drawn to the sanctuary because the body follows the heart; every believer’s heart is attached to the Kaaba in love.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r3.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} يقول: خذ بقلوب الناس إليهم فإنه حيث يهوي القلب يذهب الجسد

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says “some people” restricts the prayer to believers; otherwise Jews and Christians would also crowd Mecca. A hasan-chain route repeats this point.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لو أن إبراهيم عليه السلام حين دعا قال: اجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لازدحمت عليه اليهود والنصارى

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet praying for Medina’s people: bless their measures and make people’s hearts incline toward them.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأهل المدينة: اللهم بارك لهم في صاعهم ومدهم

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r10.claim: Abraham uses the plural Our Lord because the prayer concerns his descendants, making appeal to God’s lordship over them more likely to be accepted.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r10.anchor: والجمع لأن الآية متعلقة بذريته فالتعرض لوصف ربوبيته تعالى لهم أدخل في القبول

BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r11.claim: Some descendants means Ishmael and those descended from him, whose settlement is included in Abraham’s own settlement.
BURSEVI:v4p282#2/r11.anchor: إني أسكنت من ذريتي أي بعض ذريتي وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه فإن اسكانه متضمن لإسكانهم

BURSEVI:v4p283/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r1.claim: The barren valley is Mecca, a rocky place where nothing grows.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r1.anchor: هو وادي مكة فإنها حجرية لا تنبت أي لا يكون فيها شيء من زرع قط

BURSEVI:v4p283/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r2.claim: Like the Quran without crookedness in 39:28, the valley has no cultivation at all and only absence of growth.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r2.anchor: بمعنى لا يوجد فيه اعوجاج وما فيه إلا الاستقامة لا غير

BURSEVI:v4p283/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r3.speaker: تفسير الشيخ
BURSEVI:v4p283/r3.claim: The Shaykh’s Tafsīr describes the valley as between two mountains, with neither water nor cultivated land.

BURSEVI:v4p283/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p283/r4.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm notes that God had provided the inhabitants with running water by the commentator’s own time.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r4.anchor: وفي بحر العلوم وأما في زماننا فقد رزق الله أهله ماء جاريا

BURSEVI:v4p283/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r5.claim: The phrase is a locative adjunct of I settled; the House is the Kaaba, and its annexation to God is honorific.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r5.anchor: عند بيتك المحرم ظرف لاسكنت كقولك صليت بمكة عند الركن وهو الكعبة والاضافة للتشريف

BURSEVI:v4p283/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r6.claim: The Kaaba is sacred because God forbade harm, fighting, hunting, and entry without ihram; the Flood did not overtake it, so it is also called al-ʿAtīq, the freed one.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r6.anchor: وسمى محرما لأنه عظيم الحرمة حرم الله التعرض له بسوء يوم خلق السماوات والأرض

BURSEVI:v4p283/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p283/r7.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the sacred House as the heart, forbidden to house anything except God, invoking the saying that a believer’s heart contains Him.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r7.anchor: في التأويلات النجمية عند بيتك المحرم وهو القلب المحرم أن يكون بيتا لغير الله

BURSEVI:v4p283/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r8.claim: The repeated Our Lord displays full concern for what follows.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r8.anchor: ربنا كرر النداء لإظهار كمال العناية بما بعده

BURSEVI:v4p283/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r9.claim: The lām is purposive and attaches to I settled: Abraham settled them in this barren valley only to establish prayer, not for worldly aims; prayer is singled out for its excellence and role in reforming the soul, while Quraysh resisted it from pride.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r9.anchor: ليقيموا الصلوة اللام لام كي متعلقة باسكنت أي ما اسكنتهم بهذا الوادي البلقع

BURSEVI:v4p283/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r10.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, meaning hearts, and min is partitive.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r10.anchor: فاجعل أفئدة من الناس جمع فؤاد وهي القلوب ومن للتبعيض

BURSEVI:v4p283/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r11.claim: Tahwī means to hurry toward them in longing or fly toward them with love; hawā can mean falling rapidly, rising, or loving, with ilā expressing longing and inclination.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r11.anchor: يقال هوى يهوى من باب ضرب هويا وهويا

BURSEVI:v4p283/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283/r12.claim: The people are Ishmael and his descendants, the believers; partitive min limits the hearts drawn, whereas asking for all people would bring Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians in a crowd.
BURSEVI:v4p283/r12.anchor: أي : إسماعيل وذريته وهم المؤمنون ولو قال أفئدة الناس بدون من التبعيضة

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r1.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says one whose beauty lawfully steals the heart is worthy of love, while failing to love such beauty is a burden.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r1.anchor: وآنكس كه براننان جمالى عاشق نشود وبال باشد

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r2.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r2.claim: Mullā Jāmī’s poem depicts the sanctuary as the beloved’s gracious precinct and the qibla of beauties, drawing admirers toward it.

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r3.claim: The request includes the descendants settled there and people joining them; unlike 2:126 it is not restricted to believers because prayer has already been named.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r3.anchor: وارزقهم أي ذريتي الذين أسكنتهم هناك أو مع من ينحاز إليهم من الناس

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r4.claim: Fruit may come from nearby villages or distant lands; both happened, so spring, summer, and autumn fruits can gather in the sanctuary on one day.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r4.anchor: من الثمرات من أنواعها بأن يجعل بقرب منه قرى يحصل فيها ذلك أو يجبي إليه من الأقطار البعيدة

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Ṭāʾif, three stages from Mecca and originally part of Palestine, was lifted and placed as provision for the sanctuary after Abraham prayed.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r5.anchor: روى عن ابن عباس أن الطائف وهي على ثلاث مراحل من مكة كانت من أرض فلسطين

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r6.claim: The people should thank God for this provision through prayer and the other observances of servitude.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r6.anchor: لعلهم يشكرون تلك النعمة بإقامة الصلاة وأداء سائر مراسم العبودية

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r7.claim: Bursevī favors the view that Abraham prayed after the House was built and after arriving: the physical reference to the city and sacred House, and 14:39’s mention of Isaac, support that chronology.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r7.anchor: يقول الفقير : اختلف العلماء في أن هذا الدعاء بعد بناء البيت أو قبل أول ما قدم مكة

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r8.claim: Some say this city refers to its mental conception before it existed, since God disclosed its location; the prayer asks hearts to settle with Abraham’s descendants, not merely visit the House for pilgrimage.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الإشارة في هذا البلد إلى الموجود في الذهن قبل تحقق البلدية

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r9.claim: Bursevī objects that the pronoun does not rule out pilgrimage: the wording may elide place, meaning hearts incline to their noble place for pilgrimage, as al-Taysīr explains.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r9.anchor: يقول الفقير : فيه نظر لأنه لم لا يجوز أن يكون المعنى على حذف المضاف

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r10.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r10.claim: Al-Irshād explains calling it a House before construction by reference to its former location, then a raised mound whose floods flowed off to either side.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r10.anchor: قال في الإرشاد : تسميته إذ ذاك بيتا ولم يكن له بناء وإنما كان نشزا

BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r11.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r11.claim: Bursevī says the Kaaba’s repeated rebuilding is certain, while scholars differ over how many times it was rebuilt, citing al-Kāshifī.
BURSEVI:v4p283#2/r11.anchor: وإنما الاختلاف في كمية عدده ، كما قال الكاشفي عند

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.claim: The prayer leaves the town unnamed, either to create suspense before identifying it as the place near the Sacred House, or because Arabs knew it meant Mecca. This matches 2:126: here Abraham asks this city to be safe; there he asks that the indicated place become one of the safe cities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p237/r6.anchor: وحكاية دعائه بدون بيان البلد إبهام يرد بعده البيان بقوله : { عند بيتك المحرم ( سورة إبراهيم : 37 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.claim: ‘I have settled some of my descendants’ begins a new prayer. Its opening invocation intensifies supplication and links the invocation-led clauses as like instances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.anchor: جملة { إني أسكنت من ذريتي } مستأنفة لابتداء دعاء آخر . وافتتحت بالنداء لزيادة التضرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.claim: The invocation says ‘our Lord’ rather than the earlier ‘my Lord’ because Abraham’s prayer concerns both himself and his sons; Ishmael may be present, as the joint prayer in 2:127 suggests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.anchor: وأضيف الرب هنا إلى ضمير الجمع خلافا لسابقيه لأن الدعاء الذي افتتح به فيه حظ للداعي ولأبنائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.claim: Min means ‘some of’; the descendant is Ishmael. The prayer likely came some time after the Kaaba was built and Mecca settled, since 14:39 later mentions the gift of both Ishmael and Isaac in old age.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.anchor: ومن } في قوله : { من ذريتي } بمعنى بعض ، يعني إسماعيل عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.claim: A wādī is land between mountains; this is the valley of Mecca. ‘Without cultivation’ describes rocky land unfit for plants; dhū denotes possession and settled connection, unlike simply saying nothing grows there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.anchor: والواد : الأرض بين الجبال ، وهو وادي مكة . وغير ذي زرع } صفة ، أي بواد لا يصلح للنبت لأنه حجارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.claim: The wording parallels 39:28, ‘a Qur’an without crookedness’: the negated possessive construction means the thing is not subject to the stated quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.anchor: ولأجل هذا الاستعمال لم يقل بواد لا يزرع أولا زرع به .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.claim: ‘Near Your Sacred House’ can be a second adjective of the valley or a circumstantial phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.anchor: وعند بيتك } صفة ثانية لواد أو حال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.claim: The Sacred House is protected from harmful human interference and harm to its people by the reverence God placed in nations’ hearts, and by the destruction of those who sought wrongdoing there; the people of the Elephant were not far off.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.anchor: والمحرم : الممنع من تناول الأيدي إياه بما يفسده أو يضر أهله بما جعل الله له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.claim: The purpose phrase attaches to ‘I settled’: Abraham settled them by the House so nothing would distract them from prayer there and the House would remain continually frequented.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.anchor: وعلق { ليقيموا } ب { أسكنت } ، أي علة الإسكان بذلك الوادي عند ذلك البيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r1.claim: The vocative is placed between the opening and request to focus attention on the prayer's preamble and intensify its pleading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r1.anchor: وتوسيط النداء للاهتمام بمقدمة الدعاء زيادة في الضراعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r2.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, heart, and here means the self and intellect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r2.anchor: جمع فؤاد ، وهو القلب . والمراد به هنا النفس والعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r3.claim: The request is that people long to visit the family; mentioning hearts makes their approach seem driven by love and yearning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r3.anchor: فاجعل أناسا يهوون إليهم . فأقحم لفظ الأفئدة لإرادة أن يكون مسير الناس إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r4.claim: Min is explanatory rather than partitive, since restricting the request to only some people would add no useful point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r4.anchor: بيانية لا تبعيضية ، إذ لا طائل تحته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r5.claim: Hawā literally means to fall; here it metaphorically means to move quickly, as in Imruʾ al-Qays's image of a boulder swept down by a torrent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r5.anchor: وتهوي مضارع هوى بفتح الواو : سقط . وأطلق هنا على الإسراع في المشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r6.claim: Because hawā is used for hurrying toward them, it takes the lām construction here instead of ʿalā.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r7.claim: The haste of travel stands metonymically for love and eagerness to visit the family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r7.anchor: والإسراع : جعل كناية عن المحبة والشوق إلى زيارتهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r8.claim: The visitors are meant to make the family's home less lonely by coming regularly and meeting their needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r8.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الدعاء تأنيس مكانهم بتردد الزائرين وقضاء حوائجهم منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r9.claim: The indefinite wording is unrestricted, relying on the customary flow of visitors that sustains inhabited towns and markets; abundance need not be stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r9.anchor: والتنكير مطلق يحمل على المتعارف في عمران المدن والأسواق بالواردين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r10.claim: Love for the family brings affection for the town and repeated visits, making it familiar and encouraging its rites, which advances the religion's call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r10.anchor: ومحبة الناس إياهم يحصل معها محبة البلد وتكرير زيارته ، وذلك سبب لاستئناسهم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r11.claim: Mentioning gratitude completes the request and adds a prayer that they be grateful; provision should enable worship and remove livelihood's distracting hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p241/r11.anchor: ورجاء شكرهم داخل في الدعاء لأنه جعل تكملة له تعرضا للإجابة وزيادة في الدعاء لهم بأن يكونوا من الشاكرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r1.claim: The descendants Abraham settled are Ishmael; the phrase is partitive because Isaac remained in Syria.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r1.anchor: وقوله: من ذريتي يريد: إسماعيل عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r2.claim: A report says Abraham took Hagar and the infant on the Buraq from Syria to Mecca in one day, left them in the valley, and returned that day; the whole event was by God's revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r2.anchor: فروي أنه ركب البراق- هو وهاجر والطفل- فجاء في يوم واحد من الشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya refers readers to Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and historical accounts for the rest of Hagar and Ishmael's story.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r3.anchor: وأما كيفية بقاء هاجر وما صنعت وسائر خبر إسماعيل، ففي كتاب البخاري والسير وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r4.claim: Min is partitive because Isaac was in Syria.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r4.anchor: ومن في قوله: من ذريتي للتبعيض، لأن إسحاق كان بالشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r5.claim: A wādī is the space between two mountains and need not contain water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r5.anchor: و «الوادي» : ما بين الجبلين، وليس من شروطه أن يكون فيه ماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r6.claim: The wording implies Abraham knew God would not abandon Hagar and her son and would provide water; he says “without cultivation,” not “without water,” looking to the outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r6.anchor: ولو لم يعلم ذلك من الله لقال: غير ذي ماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r7.claim: Either the sanctuary existed before the Flood and Abraham knew it, or God had told him that He would establish a sanctuary there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r7.anchor: وإما أن يكون قالها لما كان قد أعلمه الله تعالى أنه سيبني هنالك بيتا لله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r8.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r8.claim: Qatāda and others say the sanctuary is forbidden to tyrants, who must not violate its sanctity or slight its rights.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r8.anchor: ومعنى المحرم على الجبابرة وأن تنتهك حرمته ويستخف بحقه- قاله قتادة وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r9.claim: The plural “they may establish prayer” indicates that God told Abraham the child would have descendants there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r9.anchor: وجمعه الضمير في قوله: ليقيموا يدل على أن الله قد أعلمه أن ذلك الطفل سيعقب هنالك ويكون له نسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r10.claim: The lām is most naturally purposive and attached to “I settled,” with the address to God as an interjection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r10.anchor: واللام في قوله: ليقيموا هي لام كي هذا هو الظاهر فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r11.claim: Alternatively, the lām is imperative: Abraham asks God to enable them to pray, though the wording is somewhat figurative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r11.anchor: ويصح أن تكون لام أمر، كأن رغب إلى الله أن يوفقهم بإقامة الصلاة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r12.claim: Afʾida means hearts; fuʾād is named from faʾada, and al-miftād is a fire-hearth where meat is roasted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r12.anchor: وأفئدة: القلوب، جمع فؤاد. سمي بذلك لإنفاده، مأخوذ من فأد ومنه المفتاد، وهو مستوقد النار حيث يشوى اللحم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r13.speaker: ابن عامر بخلاف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r13.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, in one transmission, reads afʾidata with an extra yāʾ after the hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بخلاف: فاجعل أفئدة بياء بعد الهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r14.claim: The account says Abraham's journey and settlement of Hagar and Ishmael were all by God's revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r14.anchor: وكان هذا كله بوحي من الله تعالى فلما ولى دعا بمضمن هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r15.claim: The narrative explains that Sarah became jealous of Hagar after Ishmael's birth, and Abraham was distressed by the two of them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p341/r15.anchor: وذلك أن سارة لما غارت بهاجر- بعد أن ولدت إسماعيل-

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r1.claim: Min al-nās is partitive and means believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r1.anchor: وقوله: من الناس تبعيض، ومراده المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r2.claim: Mujāhid says that if Abraham had prayed for the hearts of all people, Persians and Romans would have crowded the sanctuary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: لو قال إبراهيم: أفئدة الناس-

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jews and Christians would have made pilgrimage if all people had been included.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لحجته اليهود والنصارى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r4.claim: Tahwī means to travel with energetic, purposeful haste; a line by Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī witnesses the word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر [أبو كبير] : [الكامل] وإذا رميت به الفجاج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r5.claim: A transmitted verse also uses tahwī for people traveling toward Mecca seeking guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r5.anchor: ومنه البيت المروي: [السريع] تهوي إلى مكة تبغي الهدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r6.speaker: مسلمة بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r6.claim: Muslima ibn ʿAbd Allāh reads tuhwi with a ḍamma on tāʾ, from the causative verb ahwā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r6.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن عبد الله: «تهوي» بضم التاء، من أهوى، وهو الفعل المذكور معدى بالهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب ومحمد بن علي ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and Mujāhid read the verb with fatḥa on tāʾ and wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r7.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب ومحمد بن علي ومجاهد «تهوي» بفتح التاء والواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r8.claim: The verb from hawā takes ilā because here it is paired with travel and purposeful movement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r8.anchor: وتعدي هذا الفعل- وهو من الهوى- ب «إلى»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r9.speaker: مسلم بن محمد الطائفي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r9.claim: Muslim ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāʾifī reports that Gabriel carried soil from Palestine, or Jordan, circled the sanctuary seven times, and set it near Mecca; it became al-Ṭāʾif, home of Thaqīf and Rakba, with trees and fruit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342/r9.anchor: وروي عن مسلم بن محمد الطائفي: أنه لما دعا عليه السلام بأن يرزق سكان مكة من الثمرات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r1.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Farraʾ take min as partitive: Abraham settled some of his descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r1.anchor: في من قولان أحدهما أنها للتبعيض قاله الأخفش والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari takes min as emphatic, so the sense is that Abraham settled his descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها للتوكيد والمعنى أسكنت ذريتي ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r3.claim: The barren valley is Mecca, where there was no cultivation or water at the time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ بواد غير ذي زرع ﴾ يعني مكة ولم يكن فيها حرث ولا ماء عند ﴿ بيتك المحرم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r4.claim: The House is called inviolable because its prohibitions must not be violated and its due must not be treated lightly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r4.anchor: إنما سمي محرما لأنه يحرم استحلال محرماته والاستخفاف بحقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r5.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib explains the apparent anachronism by saying God had sanctified the House's site from the creation of the heavens and earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r5.anchor: أحدها أن الله تعالى حرم موضع البيت منذ خلق السموات والأرض قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r6.claim: One explanation, cited by Ibn Jarir, is that the House had existed before it was raised during the Flood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r6.anchor: والثاني عند بيتك الذي كان قبل أن يرفع أيام الطوفان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r7.claim: Another explanation cited by Ibn Jarir is that Abraham meant the House whose future appearance there was already known in God's prior decree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r7.anchor: والثالث عند بيتك الذي قد جرى في سابق علمك أنه يحدث ها هنا ذكرهما ابن جرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r8.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r8.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the wording appears to place the prayer after the House was built and Mecca became a town; Ibn al-Jawzi notes that exegetes disagree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r8.anchor: وكان أبو سليمان الدمشقي يقول ظاهر الكلام يدل على أن هذا الدعاء إنما بعد أن بني البيت وصارت مكة بلدا والمفسرون على خلاف ما قال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r9.claim: Mujahid reports that Abraham left Syria with Ishmael, Hajar, and Gabriel, found Amalekites outside Mecca and the House as a red mound, asked Gabriel if this was the commanded place, then settled them at the Hijr and told Hajar to make an enclosure before reciting this prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r9.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد أن إبراهيم خرج من الشام ومعه ابنه إسماعيل وأمه هاجر ومعه جبريل حتى قدم مكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r10.speaker: أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r10.claim: The reciters of the Hijaz and Abu Amr pronounce the yāʾ in innī askantu with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p366/r10.anchor: وفتح أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو ياء إني أسكنت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r1.claim: Muqatil connects the purpose clause to Abraham's request to keep his descendants from idol worship: he asks that they avoid idols so they can pray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة ﴾ في متعلق هذه اللام قولان أحدهما أنها تتعلق بقوله ﴿ واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r2.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r2.claim: Al-Mawardi connects the purpose clause to settling them there: Abraham placed them by the House so they could pray toward it as their qibla.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها تتعلق بقوله ﴿ أسكنت ﴾ فالمعنى أسكنتهم عند بيتك ليقيموا الصلاة لأن بيتك قبلة الصلوات ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r3.claim: Afʾidah means the hearts of a group of people; Ibn al-Anbari says the heart is called fuʾād because of its proximity and adjacency to the heart's core.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r3.anchor: أي قلوب جماعة من الناس قال ابن الأنباري وإنما عبر عن القلوب بالأفئدة لقرب القلب من الفؤاد ومجاورته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r4.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses fuʾād in the sense of heart in the line about an arrow striking it at departure.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r4.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس رمتني بسهم أصاب الفؤاد غداة الرحيل فلم أنتصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r5.speaker: آخر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r5.claim: An unnamed poet likewise uses fuʾād to mean heart, describing it as a raven's wing longing to rise toward its nest.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r5.anchor: وقال آخر كأن فؤادي كلما مر راكب جناح غراب رام نهضا إلى وكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r6.speaker: آخر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r6.claim: A second unnamed poet uses fuʾād to mean heart, saying it patiently led him into passion despite the long love.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367/r6.anchor: وقال آخر وإن فؤادا قادني لصبابة إليك على طول الهوى لصبور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains tahwī ilayhim as longing for them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r2.claim: Qatada interprets it as being drawn toward them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says it means to desire them, as when one says that someone ‘yahwī toward you,’ meaning he wants you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء تريدهم كما تقول رأيت فلانا يهوي نحوك أي يريدك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r4.claim: Some read tahwā ilayhim, meaning ‘love them,’ like the expression radifa lakum, where the preposition reinforces the wording.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ يعضهم تهوى إليهم بمعنى تهواهم كقوله ﴿ ردف لكم ﴾ النمل 72 أي ردفكم وإلى توكيد للكلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari understands the phrase as descending and settling toward them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري تهوي إليهم تنحط إليهم وتنحدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r6.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r6.claim: Most interpreters understand the attraction as people's inclination to make the pilgrimage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r6.anchor: وفي معنى هذا الميل قولان أحدهما أنه الميل إلى الحج قاله الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r7.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Atiyya says the attraction means love of living in Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه حب سكنى مكة رواه عطية عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham's wording ‘hearts of people’ would have supplied Jews and Christians with an argument, but he said ‘some people,’ restricting the request.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p367#2/r8.anchor: وروى سعيد ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال لو كان إبراهيم قال فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لحجة اليهود والنصارى ولكنه قال من الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r1.claim: This is a second prayer, after the first when Abraham left Hagar and her child before the House was built; mentioning the inviolable House marks the later prayer after its construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r1.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن هذا دعاء ثان بعد الدعاء الأول الذي دعا به عندما ولى عن هاجر وولدها، وذلك قبل بناء البيت، وهذا كان بعد بنائه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r2.claim: Ibn Jarīr says “so they may establish prayer” grammatically attaches to “the inviolable”: Abraham made the House sacred so its inhabitants could pray there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r2.anchor: قال ابن جرير: هو متعلق بقوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Saʿīd b. Jubayr say “some people” specifies Muslims: had Abraham said “the hearts of people,” Persians, Romans, Jews, Christians, and everyone would crowd there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير: لو قال: "أفئدة الناس" لازدحم عليه فارس والروم واليهود (1)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r4.claim: Abraham asks for fruit to sustain worship in the barren valley; although Mecca has no fruit-bearing trees, God brings it fruits from surrounding regions, answering his prayer in 28:57 as a kindness and blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p513/r4.anchor: ليس في البلد الحرام مكة شجرة مثمرة، وهي تجبى إليها ثمرات ما حولها، استجابة لخليله إبراهيم

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r5.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r5.claim: The common reading has tahwi with kasra on the wāw; some read it with fatḥa to mean that the hearts love them.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة: تهوي بكسر الواو، وعن بعضهم بفتح الواو بمعنى تهواهم

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r7.claim: Iskan is making a dwelling where a person can live whenever they choose.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r7.anchor: الإسكان من السكنى وهو اتخاذ مأوى لصاحبه يسكن إليه متى شاء

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r8.claim: Dhurriyya is a group of children, named either for tiny particles or for God's bringing creatures into existence.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r8.anchor: والذرية: جماعة الولد، أخذ من الذر تشبيها بها في الصغر

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r9.claim: Muharram is a place where things allowed elsewhere have been forbidden.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r9.anchor: والمحرم: الذي حرم فيه ما أحل في غيره

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r10.claim: Afʾida are the locus of the heart, singular fuʾad; al-Muʾarrij also transmits 'bellies.'

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r11.claim: Abu Muslim takes tahwi as descending or dropping down.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r11.anchor: والهوي: النزول، وتهوي تهبط، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r12.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r12.claim: Abu al-Qasim says tahwi may mean wanting to come toward someone; hawa can mean love.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r12.anchor: تهوي تريد، يقال: فلان يهوي نحوك أي: يريد أن يأتيك، عن أبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r1.claim: The object of asqantu is omitted, estimated as 'people' or 'a child' from my descendants, per Abu al-Qasim.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r1.anchor: قيل: محذوف تقديره: من ذريتي أناسا، عن أبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r2.claim: The descendants are Ishmael and his mother Hagar, without disagreement; he was Abraham's eldest and helped raise the House's foundations.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r2.anchor: ولا خلاف أنه إسماعيل مع أمه هاجر وهو أكبر ولده

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r3.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the reference is Ishmael and his descendants.

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r4.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r4.claim: Al-Asamm explains the wording by saying Isaac had already been born, though another view says he had not.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r4.anchor: قال الأصم: وإنما قال: (من ذريتي) لأن إسحاق كان يومئذ قد ولد

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r5.claim: At that time the valley had no water, crops, or livestock.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r5.anchor: لأنه لم يكن بها يومئذ ماء ولا زرع ولا ضرع

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r6.claim: Abu ʿAli says Abraham attributed the House to God because he was commanded to honor it; another view says God alone owns it.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r6.anchor: أضافه إليه لأنه تعبد بتعظيمه، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r7.claim: A future house may be called God's House when its existence and boundaries are already known; alternatives identify the pre-Flood House or one decreed in prior knowledge.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r7.anchor: إذا كان المعلوم كونه وعرف حده جاز أن يقال: بيتك

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the House's precinct was made sacred at creation and surrounded by seven angels.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r8.anchor: حرم موضع البيت حين خلق السماوات والأرض، وحفه بسبعة أملاك، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r9.claim: Abu ʿAli says blood and filth were forbidden there and pilgrims were ordered into ihram from things previously lawful.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r9.anchor: حرم على عباده أن يقربوه الدماء والأقذار وغيرها، ولأنه أمر الصائرين إليه

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r10.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r10.claim: Al-Qadi says the House has a special sanctity in several respects; other views say it cannot be owned or overpowered by a tyrant.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r10.anchor: بما له من الحرمة الخاصة من جهات، عن القاضي

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r11.claim: Abraham settled his family there so they could establish prayer; one gloss says they would pray toward the Kaaba.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r11.anchor: بين أنه أسكنهم ليقيموا الصلاة، وقيل: ليقيموها نحو الكعبة

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r12.claim: Abraham asks for religious and worldly benefit: without God's gentleness in turning hearts, the barren place could not sustain them; people visit for worship or trade by His grace.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r12.anchor: ثم دعا بجامع الدين والدنيا، فقال سبحانه: فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says 'some people' means Muslims; otherwise Jews, Christians, and Magians would have made pilgrimage.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r13.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لو قال أفئدة الناس لحجت اليهود والنصارى والمجوس

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r14.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r14.claim: Mujahid says if Abraham had asked for the hearts of all people, Persia and Rome would have crowded to Mecca.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r14.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن إبراهيم لو قال لازدحمت فارس والروم

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r15.claim: Afʾida means hearts, so the prayer asks that the family be made beloved in people's hearts.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r15.anchor: الأفئدة القلوب، أي: حببهم في قلوب الناس

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والزجاج
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and al-Zajjaj take tahwi as inclining toward them.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r16.anchor: يقال: هوى نحوه إذا مال، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والزجاج

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r18.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r18.claim: Abu Muslim says the hearts descend to Mecca because it lies in a hollow.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r18.anchor: تنزل وتهبط إليهم لأن مكة في غور، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r19.speaker: عطاء وطاووس
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r19.claim: ʿAtaʾ and Tawus say people come to the House with their hearts inclined to it.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r19.anchor: يأتون البيت تهوي إليهم قلوبهم، عن عطاء، وطاووس

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r20.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r20.claim: Al-Hasan says Abraham asked that pilgrimage be made beloved to God's servants, and God answered by making it obligatory; another gloss specifies Hajj and ʿUmra.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r20.anchor: سأله أن يحبب الحج إلى عباده فأجاب وأوجب الحج

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r21.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r21.claim: Abu ʿAli says he asked God to incline hearts so the family could find company and receive provisions.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r21.anchor: أمل قلوبهم إليه ليأنسوا بها وينقلوا الميرة إليهم، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r22.claim: Fruits are brought from distant regions as visitors arrive, or are carried there as settlements grow, so that the family may thank God.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r22.anchor: وارزقهم من الثمرات مما يجلب إليهم من الأقطار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r1.claim: The descendants settled there are some of Abraham's children: Ishmael and his offspring.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r1.anchor: بعض أولادي وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r2.claim: The valley is the valley of Mecca.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r3.claim: It means that no crop grows there at all, like “without crookedness” in 39:28, meaning there is no crookedness whatsoever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r3.anchor: لا يكون فيه شيء من زرع قط ، كقوله : { قرءانا عربيا غير ذي عوج }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r4.claim: The House is called forbidden because God prohibited its violation and sanctified its surroundings, because it has always been protected from tyrants, because it is sacred and inviolable, or because it was spared the Flood, like its name ʿAtīq (“freed”).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r4.anchor: وقيل للبيت المحرم ، لأن الله حرم التعرض له والتهاون به ، وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r5.claim: The purpose phrase attaches to “I settled”: Abraham placed them in this barren, unprovided valley only to establish prayer at the sacred House.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r5.anchor: اللام متعلقة بأسكنت ، أي : ما أسكنتهم هذا الوادي الخلاء البلقع من كل مرتفق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r6.claim: Their purpose is to worship and remember God at the honored site, approach Him through staying, circumambulation, bowing, and prostration, and seek the mercy granted to sanctuary residents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r6.anchor: ويعمروه بذكرك وعبادتك وما تعمر به مساجدك ومتعبداتك ، متبركين بالبقعة التي شرفتها على البقاع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r7.claim: Min is partitive: Abraham asks for some people's hearts; Mujahid says that without min, Persians and Romans would crowd the site.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r7.anchor: ومن للتبعيض ، ويدل عليه ما روي عن مجاهد : لو قال أفئدة الناس لزحمتكم عليه فارس والروم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r8.claim: Another view says min is for origin, as in “the heart is sick in me,” yielding “hearts of people”; the indefinite wording still means only some hearts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { من } للابتداء ، كقولك : القلب مني سقيم ، تريد قلبي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r9.claim: The reading āfida is explained either by metathesis, as in ādir from adʾur, or as an active form from afadat, “the journey hastened,” meaning groups hurrying toward them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r9.anchor: وقرىء : ( آفدة ) ، بوزن عاقدة . وفيه وجهان ، أحدهما : أن يكون من القلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r10.claim: A reading afida is explained either as hamza dropped for ease, though intermediate pronunciation is more usual, or as derived from afada.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r10.anchor: وقرىء : ( أفدة ) ، وفيه وجهان : أن تطرح الهمزة للتخفيف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r11.claim: The hearts hasten and fly toward them in longing, as illustrated by the poetic phrase “yahwī makhārimahā hawā al-ajdal.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p524/r11.anchor: { تهوى إليهم } تسرع إليهم وتطير نحوهم شوقا ونزاعا من قوله :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r1.claim: One reading is passive, from hawā ilayhi and ahwāhu (another caused it to incline); another reads active hawā, “love,” with the verb carrying the sense of tanziʿ and taking its construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r1.anchor: وقرىء : ( تهوى إليهم ) ، على البناء للمفعول ، من هوى إليه وأهواه غيره . وتهوى إليهم ، من هوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r2.claim: Though the valley has no fruit, God can bring fruit there from other lands so its people may give thanks.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r2.anchor: { وارزقهم من الثمرات } مع سكناهم واديا ما فيه شيء منها ، بأن تجلب إليهم من البلاد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r3.claim: God answered by making the valley a safe sanctuary supplied with fruits of every kind; its marvel is that fruits from different seasons ripen there together in one day, surpassing fertile lands.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525/r3.anchor: لا جرم أن الله عز وجل أجاب دعوته فجعله حرما آمنا تجبى إليه . ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Taif was originally in Palestine; after Abraham's prayer, God lifted it and placed it where it is as provision for the sanctuary.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : كانت الطائف من أرض فلسطين ، فلما قال إبراهيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r1.claim: These are Abraham's words; the descendants he means are Ishmael and his mother Hagar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r1.anchor: هذا قول إبراهيم عليه السلام . وقوله { من ذريتي } يريد بهم إسماعيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r2.claim: The barren valley is Mecca; Abraham settled them in its open valley, which had no inhabitants, trusting in God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r2.anchor: يعني مكة أسكنها في بطحائها , ولم يكن بها ساكن , ثقة بالله وتوكلا عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r3.claim: Abraham settled them by the House because it is the prayer direction; the House is God's alone and is sacred because acts such as sexual intercourse are forbidden there though permitted elsewhere.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r3.anchor: لأنه قبلة الصلوات فلذلك أسكنهم عنده . وأضاف البيت إليه لأنه لا يملكه غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r4.claim: One reading of the purpose is that Abraham asks God to guide them to establish prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r4.anchor: أن يكون سأل الله تعالى بذلك أن يهديهم إلى إقامة الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r5.claim: A second reading is that prayer explains why Abraham left them there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r5.anchor: أن يكون ذكر سبب تركهم فيه أن يقيموا الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r6.claim: Afʾida can be the plural of fuʾād, meaning hearts; a cited poem uses fuʾād for the heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r6.anchor: أن الأفئدة جمع فؤاد وهي القلوب , وقد يعبر عن القلب بالفؤاد , قال الشاعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r7.claim: Another possibility takes afʾida as a plural of wafd, meaning delegations from nations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r7.anchor: فكأنه قال : فاجعل وفودا من الأمم تهوي إليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r8.claim: One gloss takes tahwī as longing or yearning toward them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r9.claim: A second gloss takes it as descending to them, since Mecca lies in a valley and visitors descend toward it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r9.anchor: لأن مكة في واد والقاصد إليها نازل إليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r10.claim: A third gloss takes it as rising toward them, since what leaves the heart is as though lifted away from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r10.anchor: لأن ما في القلوب بخروجه منها كالمرتفع عنها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r11.claim: A fourth gloss takes the phrase to mean that people love them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r12.claim: A variant reading is tahwā, rather than tahwī.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham asked for hearts to long to live in Mecca, making it a sacred city.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r13.anchor: أحدهما : ليهووا السكنى بمكة فيصير بلدا محرما , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid say Abraham asked that people be drawn to Mecca to perform pilgrimage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r14.anchor: فيحجوا , قاله سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that without the words 'from among people,' Jews, Christians, Persians, and Romans would all have made pilgrimage there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لولا أنه قال من الناس لحجه اليهود والنصارى وفارس والروم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r16.claim: One view takes the fruits as fruits of the heart: God makes them beloved so people visit them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r16.anchor: يريد ثمرات القلوب بأن تحببهم إلى قلوب الناس فيزوروهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r17.claim: A second view means literal fruits of palms and trees; God answered with produce from Taif and imports from other regions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r17.anchor: الثاني : ومن الظاهر من ثمرات النخل والأشجار , فأجابه بما في الطائف من الثمار

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p137#4/r18.claim: The phrase means 'so that they may thank You.'

MUJAHID:v1p337#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p337#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p337#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had Abraham asked for all people's hearts to incline to his descendants, Jews and Christians would have made pilgrimage; saying 'some people' specified believers.
MUJAHID:v1p337#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لو أن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن قال فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لحجه اليهود والنصارى

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r6.claim: The descendants were Ishmael in particular; the barren, waterless valley was Mecca.

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r7.claim: God made the House sacred against unlawful acts; Muqatil notes fronting in the clause, whose purpose is that they pray and worship there.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r7.anchor: حرمه لئلا يستحل فيه ما لا يحل

MUQATIL:14:35-37/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r8.claim: Ibrahim asks that some people yearn toward Ishmael and his descendants and that they receive fruits; specifying some avoids crowding by Haraz and Daylam.
MUQATIL:14:35-37/r8.anchor: ولو قال: اجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r1.claim: The descendants Abraham settled were some of his children: Ishmael and his descendants.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r1.anchor: بعض أولادى وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r2.claim: The valley is Mecca, where nothing grows at all.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ بواد ﴾ هو وادى مكة ﴿ غير ذي زرع ﴾ لا يكون فيه شيء من زرع قط

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r3.claim: The Sacred House is named so because God forbade treating it carelessly and made its surroundings sacred for its sake.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r3.anchor: لأن الله تعالى حرم التعرض له والتهاون به وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is named because it has always been protected from every tyrant.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r4.anchor: أو لأنه لم يزل ممنعا يها به كل جبار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is revered and possesses a great sanctity that may not be violated.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r5.anchor: أو لأنه محترم عظيم الحرمة لا يحل انتهاكها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r6.claim: Alternatively, it is protected from the flood, just as it is called ʿAtīq because it was freed from it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r6.anchor: أو لأنه حرم على الطوفان أي منع منه كما سمى عتيقا لأنه أعتق منه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r7.claim: The purpose phrase li-yuqīmū is attached to askantu: Abraham settled them in the barren valley solely to establish prayer at the Sacred House and maintain it through worship and remembrance.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r7.anchor: اللام متعلقة باسكنت أي ما اسكنتهم بهذا الوادى البلقع إلا ليقيموا الصلاة عند بيتك المحرم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r8.claim: Min is partitive: Abraham asks for some human hearts, since asking for all hearts would have brought Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians to crowd the place.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r8.anchor: ومن للتبعيض لما روى عن مجاهد لو قال أفئدة الناس لزاحمتكم عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r9.claim: Mujāhid says that had Abraham asked for all people's hearts, Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians would have crowded there.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد لو قال أفئدة الناس لزاحمتكم عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r10.claim: Min may instead mark origin, as in saying my heart is sick; the phrase then means people's hearts, with the possessor indefinite to match the indefinite afʾida.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p232#3/r10.anchor: أو للابتداء كقولك القلب منى سقيم تريد قلبى فكانه قيل أفئدة ناس

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r1.claim: The hearts rush to Abraham's descendants from distant lands, flying toward them with longing.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r1.anchor: تسرع اليهم من البلاد الشاسعة وتطير نحوهم شوقا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r2.claim: Although they live in a valley with no fruit, God supplies them by bringing fruit from faraway lands.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r2.anchor: مع سكناهم واديا ما فيه شيء منها بأن تجلب إليهم من البلاد الشاسعة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r3.claim: They may give thanks for the provision of many kinds of fruit in a valley without trees or water.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233/r3.anchor: النعمة في أن يرزقوا أنواع الثمرات في واد ليس فيه شجر ولا ماء

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r1.claim: The Bukhari report from Ibn Abbas recounts Abraham leaving nursing Hajar and Ismail at the House near Zamzam with dates and water, at an empty, waterless valley; Hajar trusted God after confirming the command.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أول ما اتخذ النساء المنطق من قبل أم إسمعيل

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r2.claim: In the same report, Hajar runs seven times between Safa and Marwa as the child suffers from thirst; the Prophet identifies this as the people’s saʿy.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r3.claim: The report says an angel excavated Zamzam at Gabriel’s place, and Hajar gathered water while it flowed; the Prophet says that had she left it, Zamzam would have been a running spring.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37/r3.anchor: فإذا هي بالملك عند موضع زمزم فبحث بعقبه أو قال بجناحه حتى ظهر الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r1.speaker: الملك
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r1.claim: The angel reassures Hajar that there is no danger of loss: the boy and his father will build God’s House, and God will not abandon its people.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r1.anchor: فقال لها الملك: لا تخافي الضيعة فإن هاهنا بيت الله يبنيه هذا الغلام وأبوه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r2.claim: One may not abandon children and family in a desolate place by appealing to this story, trusting God, or following extreme Sufi claims about true reliance: Abraham acted on God’s command.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r2.anchor: لا يجوز لأحد أن يتعلق بهذا في طرح ولده وعياله بأرض مضيعة اتكالا على العزيز الرحيم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r3.claim: A report says Sarah’s jealousy after Hajar bore Ismail led Abraham to bring Hajar and the child to Mecca; another says they traveled by Buraq from Syria in one day, all by revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي أن سارة لما غارت من هاجر بعد أن ولدت إسمعيل خرج بها إبراهيم عليه السلام إلى مكة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r4.claim: As God established the place for the honored House and sacred city, He sent the angel to uncover water and make it nourishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r4.anchor: لما أراد الله تأسيس الحال، وتمهيد المقام، وخط الموضع للبيت المكرم، والبلد المحرم، أرسل الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r5.claim: In an authentic report, Abu Dharr says Zamzam water alone sustained him for thirty days and nights; he gained weight and felt no pang of hunger.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r5.anchor: وفي الصحيح: أن أبا ذر رضي الله عنه اجتزأ به ثلاثين بين يوم وليلة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas transmitted by al-Daraqutni says Zamzam serves the drinker’s intention: healing, satiety, or relief from thirst; it is Gabriel’s digging and God’s water for Ismail.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
