QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r7.claim: Ikrima reports that Ibn Abbas prayed for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every disease when drinking Zamzam.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r7.anchor: وروي أيضا عن عكرمة قال: كان ابن عباس إذا شرب من زمزم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Zamzam’s promised benefits remain until the Last Day for the sincere person of sound inner character who drinks in trust rather than testing it; God exposes those who experiment.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهذا موجود فيه إلى يوم القيامة لمن صحت نيته، وسلمت طويته

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi recounts that on a crowded, dark pilgrimage night he drank deeply from Zamzam to avoid leaving the circumambulation for a need, and the discomfort disappeared until morning.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي وحدثني أبي رحمه الله قال: دخلت الطواف في ليلة ظلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r10.claim: A report from Abdullah ibn Amr says a spring in Paradise lies at Zamzam from the direction of the corner.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r10.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن عمرو: إن في زمزم عينا في الجنة من قبل الركن

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r11.claim: Min in “some of my descendants” is partitive: Abraham settled some of his descendants, namely Ismail and his mother, since Isaac was in Syria.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r11.anchor: «من» في قوله تعالى: «من ذريتي» للتبعيض أي أسكنت بعض ذريتي يعني إسمعيل وأمه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r12.claim: Another grammatical view treats min as an extra particle, yielding “I settled my descendants.”
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: هي صلة أي أسكنت ذريتي

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r13.claim: The verse indicates that the House existed from ancient times, as in reports placing it before the Flood; Abraham attributes it to God because no one else owns it.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r13.anchor: يدل على أن البيت كان قديما على ما روي قبل الطوفان، وقد مضى هذا المعنى في سورة «البقرة»

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r14.claim: Muharram can mean that acts permitted elsewhere, such as sex, are forbidden there; another view says it is protected from tyrants and violation of its sanctity, as Qatadah and others say.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r14.anchor: ووصفه بأنه محرم، أي يحرم فيه ما يستباح في غيره من جماع واستحلال. وقيل: محرم على الجبابرة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r15.claim: Prayer is singled out from the religion because of its merit and rank; it is God’s covenant with His servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#2/r15.anchor: خصها من جملة الدين لفضلها فيه، ومكانها منه، وهي عهد الله عند العباد

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r1.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that God prescribed five prayers for His servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r1.anchor: خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على العباد

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r2.claim: The apparent parsing makes li in li-yuqimu al-salah a purpose particle attached to “I settled.”
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r2.anchor: واللام في «ليقيموا الصلاة» لام كي هذا هو الظاهر فيها وتكون متعلقة ب «أسكنت»

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, li may be a command particle, as though Abraham asks God to entrust them and enable them to establish prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r3.anchor: ويصح أن تكون لام أمر، كأنه رغب إلى الله أن يأتمنهم و أن يوفقهم لإقامة الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r4.claim: The verse indicates that prayer in Mecca is superior, since Abraham settled them by the sacred House so they would pray there.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r4.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية أن الصلاة بمكة أفضل من الصلاة بغيرها لأن معنى «ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة»

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r5.speaker: أهل الأثر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r5.claim: Most hadith scholars prefer prayer in the Sacred Mosque to prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque by one hundred prayers, citing Ibn al-Zubayr’s Prophetic report; the commentator calls its wording sound and its transmission trustworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r5.anchor: فذهب عامة أهل الأثر إلى أن الصلاة في المسجد الحرام أفضل من الصلاة في مسجد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بمائة صلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r6.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r6.claim: Abu Umar authenticates the Ibn al-Zubayr report through Habib al-Muallim from Ata: Yahya ibn Maʿin, Ahmad, and Abu Zurʿa call Habib trustworthy, and Abu Hatim al-Busti includes the report in his Sahih; the commentator treats it as decisive evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r6.anchor: وقد خرج حديث حبيب المعلم هذا عن عطاء بن أبي رباح عن عبد الله بن الزبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r7.claim: Abu Umar also cites a similar Prophetic report from Ibn Umar via Musa al-Juhani and Nafi; Musa is deemed trustworthy and praised by al-Qattan, Ahmad, and Yahya.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وقد روي عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل حديث ابن الزبير

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r1.claim: The prophetic report traced to Jabir in the preceding segment says prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque is better than a thousand elsewhere, while prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than one hundred thousand elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r1.anchor: صلاة في مسجدي هذا أفضل من ألف صلاة فيما سواه إلا المسجد الحرام وصلاة في المسجد الحرام أفضل من مائة ألف فيما سواه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r2.speaker: حكيم بن سيف
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r2.claim: Hakim ibn Sayf’s Jabir transmission is judged by Abu Umar to be acceptable; if its narrator preserved it, these are two reports, otherwise Habib al-Muallim’s wording prevails.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r2.anchor: وحكيم بن سيف هذا شيخ من أهل الرقة قد روى عنه أبو زرعة الرازي، وأخذ عنه ابن وضاح

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r3.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r3.claim: Abu Umar says the cited reports decisively settle the dispute for anyone guided rightly and free of partisanship.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وهذا كله نص في موضع الخلاف قاطع له عند من ألهم رشده، ولم تمل به عصبيته

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r4.claim: Afʾidah is the plural of fuʾad, meaning hearts; the word fuʾad can stand for qalb, as the quoted poem demonstrates.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r4.anchor: الأفئدة جمع فؤاد وهي القلوب، وقد يعبر عن القلب بالفؤاد كما قال الشاعر

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r5.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r5.claim: The cited poet’s line uses fuʾad for the heart and shows it being led by longing.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r5.anchor: وإن فؤادا قادني بصبابة إليك على طول المدى لصبور

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r6.claim: Another view derives afʾidah from wafd, “delegation”: from the original awfidah, the fa is advanced and the waw changes to ya, yielding “delegations of people.”
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r6.anchor: وقيل: جمع وفد، والأصل أوفدة، فقدمت الفاء وقلبت الواو ياء كما هي

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r7.claim: Hawiya means to incline toward; the verb also describes a she-camel running swiftly as if into the air of a well, which explains the wording here.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r7.anchor: يقال: هوي نحوه إذا مال، وهوت الناقة تهوي هويا فهي هاوية إذا عدت عدوا شديدا

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say the phrase “hearts of the people” without min would draw Persians, Romans, Turks, Indians, Jews, Christians, and Magians; min restricts the yearning to Muslims, who long to visit the House.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند واليهود والنصارى والمجوس

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r9.claim: Mujahid reads tahwā ilayhim, taking it to mean that people love and revere them.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r9.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد «تهوى إليهم» أي تهواهم وتجلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r10.claim: God answered the prayer by growing the trees of al-Taif and bringing fruits to Mecca from other lands.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r10.anchor: فاستجاب الله دعاءه، وأنبت لهم بالطائف سائر الأشجار، وبما يجلب إليهم من الأمصار

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r11.claim: A report via Yusuf ibn Adi from Ibn Umar says prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque is better than a thousand elsewhere except the Sacred Mosque, where prayer is better than elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r11.anchor: حدثنا يوسف بن عدي عن عمر بن عبيد عن عبد الملك عن عطاء عن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r12.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r12.claim: Ibn Habib says Mutarrif and Asbagh, reporting from Ibn Wahb, preferred the Sacred Mosque over the Prophet’s Mosque based on reports in this chapter.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r12.anchor: وذكر ابن حبيب عن مطرف وعن أصبغ

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r13.speaker: مالك وسائر العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r13.claim: Malik and the other scholars agree that Eid prayers are held in an open area in every town except Mecca, where they are held in the Sacred Mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r13.anchor: وقد اتفق مالك وسائر العلماء على أن صلاة العيدين يبرز لهما في كل بلد إلا مكة فإنها تصلى في المسجد الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r14.speaker: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وأبو الدرداء وجابر
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r14.claim: Umar, Ali, Ibn Masud, Abu al-Darda, and Jabir preferred Mecca and its mosque; the commentator says they are more worthy to follow, and attributes this view to al-Shafiʿi, Ata, Meccans, Kufans, and a report from Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r14.anchor: وكان عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وأبو الدرداء وجابر يفضلون مكة ومسجدها وهم أولى بالتقليد ممن بعدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r15.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r15.claim: A report from Malik in Ibn Wahb’s Jamiʿ says Adam asked which place God most preferred for worship and was told Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r15.anchor: ذكر ابن وهب في جامعه عن مالك أن آدم عليه السلام لما أهبط إلى الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r16.speaker: مالك وأهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r16.claim: The well-known view of Malik and the people of Medina prefers Medina; Basrans and Baghdadis disagreed, with some favoring Mecca and others Medina.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r16.anchor: والمشهور عنه وعن أهل المدينة تفضيل المدينة، واختلف أهل البصرة والبغداديون في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r17.claim: At the end of this segment, the commentator introduces a long Bukhari report from Ibn Abbas, continued in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#4/r17.anchor: في صحيح البخاري عن ابن عباس الحديث الطويل وقد ذكرنا بعضه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r1.claim: The Bukhari report from Ibn Abbas tells how Abraham visited after Ismail’s first marriage: the wife complained of hardship, so Abraham left a message to change the doorstep; Ismail understood and divorced her.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r1.anchor: فجاء إبراهيم بعد ما تزوج إسمعيل يطالع تركته فلم يجد إسمعيل

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r2.claim: In the same report, Abraham’s second daughter-in-law praises their provision of meat and water; he asks God to bless them, and the Prophet says they had no grain, which Abraham would also have blessed.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r2.anchor: ما طعامكم؟ قالت: اللحم. قال فما شرابكم؟ قالت: الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham asked that people yearn to settle in Mecca so it would become a sanctuary.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قول إبراهيم { فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم } سأل أن يجعل الله الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r4.claim: The Bukhari account says Jurhum were the first to settle there: a caravan saw a bird circling, found Zamzam, and asked Hajar permission to camp, agreeing they had no right to the water; she welcomed company.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#5/r4.anchor: وأول من سكنه جرهم. ففي البخاري بعد قوله: وإن الله لا يضيع أهله وكان البيت مرتفعا من الأرض كالرابية

QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#6/r1.claim: The Bukhari report continues that Hajar welcomed the company because she wanted companionship; Jurhum settled there with their families, Ismail grew up, and Hajar died before Abraham later visited him.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:37#6/r1.anchor: فألفى ذلك أم إسمعيل وهي تحب الأنس

QASHANI:14:35-38/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r7.claim: The offspring are the faculties; the barren valley is bodily nature, devoid of planting in perception, knowledge, gnosis, or virtue, and the forbidden house is the heart.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r7.anchor: أي: وادي الطبيعة الجسمانية الخالية عن زرع الإدراك والعلم والمعرفة والفضيلة

QASHANI:14:35-38/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r8.claim: Their prayer is the prayer of intimate communion and unveiling.

QASHANI:14:35-38/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r9.claim: The hearts are the human senses, which distinguish the faculties through sensation, supply particular perceptions, and incline to support them through bodily pleasures and the lower direction.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r9.anchor: فتميزهم بأنواع الإحساسات وتمدهم بإدراك الجزئيات

QASHANI:14:35-38/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r10.claim: The fruits are universal knowledge and realities, and gratitude means using those perceptions in pursuit of perfection.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r10.anchor: نعمتك فيستعملون تلك المدركات في طلب الكمال

RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r1.claim: Among Abraham's requests, security comes first, showing it is the greatest blessing: religious and worldly interests cannot be completed without it.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r1.anchor: والابتداء بطلب نعمة الأمن في هذا الدعاء يدل على أنه أعظم أنواع النعم والخيرات وأنه لا يتم شيء من مصالح الدين والدنيا إلا به

RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r2.claim: Asked whether security or health is better, a scholar chose security: a sheep with a broken leg eventually grazes again, but fear of a nearby wolf keeps it from eating until it dies.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107/r2.anchor: وسئل بعض العلماء الأمن أفضل أم الصحة ؟ فقال : الأمن أفضل

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r1.claim: “Some of my descendants” means a portion of Abraham's descendants: Ishmael and those born from him.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r1.anchor: فقوله : { من ذريتي } أي بعض ذريتي وهو إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r2.claim: The valley without cultivation is the valley of Mecca, containing no crops; the phrase “without crookedness” in Qur'an 39:28 is a parallel usage.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r2.anchor: وادي مكة { غير ذى زرع } أي ليس فيه شيء من زرع

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r3.claim: One explanation of “the sacred House” is that God forbade aggression and disrespect toward it and made the surrounding area sacred because of it.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r3.anchor: الأول : أن الله حرم التعرض له والتهاون به ، وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r4.claim: A second explanation says it was always impregnable and feared by every tyrant, like something forbidden that must be avoided.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r4.anchor: أنه كان لم يزل ممتنعا عزيزا يهابه كل جبار كالشيء المحرم الذي حقه أن يجتنب

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r5.claim: A third explanation derives the name from its honored status and great inviolability.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r5.anchor: سمي محرما لأنه محترم عظيم الحرمة لا يحل انتهاكه

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r6.claim: A fourth explanation says the House was protected from the flood, as the name al-ʿAtīq reflects its being freed from the flood's dominance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r6.anchor: أنه حرم على الطوفان أي امتنع منه كما سمي عتيقا لأنه أعتق منه فلم يستعل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r7.claim: A fifth explanation links the name to pilgrims being commanded to enter consecration, abstaining from things previously lawful to them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r7.anchor: أمر الصائرين إليه أن يحرموا على أنفسهم أشياء كانت تحل لهم من قبل

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r8.claim: A sixth explanation says the site was made sacred at the creation of the heavens and earth, surrounded by seven angels; Adam built its counterpart, al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then it was raised to the seventh heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r8.anchor: السادس : حرم موضع البيت حين خلق السموات والأرض وحفه بسبعة من الملائكة ، وهو مثل البيت المعمور الذي بناه آدم

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r9.claim: A seventh explanation says people were forbidden to approach the House with blood, filth, and similar impurities.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r9.anchor: حرم على عباده أن يقربوه بالدماء والأقذار وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r10.claim: A report recounts Sarah giving her servant Hajar to Abraham, Hajar bearing Ishmael, and Sarah asking Abraham to take the nursing child and mother away; he settled them at Mecca and entrusted them to God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r10.anchor: روي أن هاجر كانت أمة لسارة فوهبتها لإبراهيم عليه السلام فولدت له إسماعيل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r11.claim: The Prophet said, “May God have mercy on Ismail's mother”; had she not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r11.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( رحم الله أم إسماعيل لولا أنها عجلت لكانت زمزم عينا معينا )

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r12.claim: The account continues that Abraham returned after Ishmael grew, and he and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r12.anchor: ثم إن إبراهيم عليه السلام عاد بعد كبر إسماعيل واشتغل هو مع إسماعيل برفع قواعد البيت

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r13.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r13.claim: Al-Qāḍī regards much of the story as implausible: Abraham would not place his child where there was no food or water if another Syrian town was available, unless God had told him provisions would appear.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r13.anchor: قال القاضي : أكثر الأمور المذكورة في هذه الحكاية بعيدة لأنه لا يجوز لإبراهيم عليه السلام أن ينقل ولده إلى حيث لا طعام ولا ماء

RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r14.claim: Razi says Zamzam's appearance could be an irhāṣ, a prophetic foretoken for Ishmael, which he permits; the Muʿtazila instead call it a miracle for Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v19p107#2/r14.anchor: وأقول : أما ظهور ماء زمزم فيحتمل أن يكون إرهاصا لإسمعيل عليه السلام ، لأن ذلك عندنا جائز خلافا للمعتزلة

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r1.claim: The purpose phrase “so that they establish prayer” attaches to “I settled”: Abraham settled Ishmael and his children in the barren valley for prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r1.anchor: واللام متعلقة بأسكنت أي أسكنت قوما من ذريتي ، وهم إسماعيل وأولاده بهذا الوادي الذي لا زرع فيه ليقيموا الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r2.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says hawā yahwī hawyan, with fatḥa, means to fall from a height to a lower place; other reported senses are to desire, hasten, descend, or come down toward them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r2.anchor: قال الأصمعي هوى يهوي هويا بالفتح إذا سقط من علو إلى سفل . وقيل : { تهوى إليهم } تريدهم ، وقيل : تسرع إليهم

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r3.claim: This prayer joins religious and worldly aims: people travel there for rites and obedience, and commerce brings livelihoods, expanding food, clothing, and general living conditions.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r3.anchor: أن هذا الدعاء جامع للدين والدنيا . أما الدين فلأنه يدخل فيه ميل الناس إلى الذهاب إلى تلك البلدة

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r4.claim: “Some” is partitive: Abraham asks for the hearts of some people to incline toward his family.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r4.anchor: كلمة { من } في قوله : { فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوى إليهم } تفيد التبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r5.claim: Mujāhid says that if Abraham had said all people's hearts, Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians would have crowded there.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد : لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says that if Abraham had said all people's hearts, Jews, Christians, and Magians would have made pilgrimage; “some” means Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : لو قال أفئدة الناس ، لحجت اليهود والنصارى المجوس

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r7.claim: Saying “some of the fruits” rather than “the fruits” indicates that Abraham asked for a portion of the fruits to reach them.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r7.anchor: أنه لم يقل : وارزقهم الثمرات ، بل قال : { وارزقهم من الثمرات } وذلك يدل على أن المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r8.claim: The fruits may reach Mecca through trade, or through cultivation in nearby villages from which produce is brought.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r8.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد بإيصال الثمرات إليهم إيصالها إليهم على سبيل التجارات

RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r9.claim: Abraham seeks worldly provisions for his descendants so they can devote themselves to prayer, worship, and fulfilling their obligations.
RAZI-FULL:v19p108/r9.anchor: فإن إبراهيم عليه السلام بين أنه إنما طلب تيسير المنافع على أولاده لأجل أن يتفرغوا لإقامة الصلوات وأداء الواجبات

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r15.claim: Abraham’s statement that he settled his family there expresses truthful reliance on God and delegation to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r15.anchor: أخبر عن صدق توكله وصدق تفويضه بقوله : { إني أسكنت }

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r16.claim: He saw their care as lying in proximity to the House, rather than in worldly provision.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r16.anchor: وإنما رأى الرفق بهم في الجوار لا في المبار قال : { عند بيتك المحرم }

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r17.claim: He settled them to establish God’s right, rather than to pursue their own interests.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r17.anchor: ثم قال : { ليقيموا الصلاة } : أي أسكنتم لإقامة حقك لطلب حظوظهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r18.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r18.claim: Another reading says Abraham was content for his family to live under God’s care rather than under the shade of worldly blessings.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r18.anchor: ويقال اكتفى أن يكونوا في ظلال عنايته عن أن يكونوا في ظلال نعمته

QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r19.claim: Abraham asks that people’s hearts incline toward his family so they can devote themselves to worship, while God sustains them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p126/r19.anchor: أي ليشتغلوا بعبادتك ، وأقم قومي - ما بقوا - بكفايتك

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r1.claim: Whoever fulfills God’s right is answered by God’s care for his people; hearts across land and sea become naturally inclined to love the House’s lineage, residents, and associates.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r1.anchor: فإن من قام بحق الله أقام الله بحقه قومه ، واستجاب الله دعاءه فيهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r2.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r2.claim: The barren valley signifies a place where hearts do not attach to worldly others and minds and inner selves are not occupied by anything else.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r2.anchor: أسكنتهم بهذا الوادي حتى لا تتعلق بالأغيار قلوبهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r3.claim: The family are cast at God’s door, protected in His presence, and bound by His decree; cared for, they are honored, but rejected, they are utterly weak.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r3.anchor: فهم مطروحون ببابك ، مصونون بحضرتك ، مرتبطون بحكمك

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r1.claim: One interpretation takes Abraham's progeny here to mean his son Ishmael.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r1.anchor: Some of my progeny can be a reference to Abraham’s son Ishmael

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r2.claim: Another interpretation understands Abraham's progeny here as Ishmael together with his mother Hagar.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r2.anchor: or to Ishmael and his mother, Hagar

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r3.claim: The uncultivated valley is Makkah, and the Sacred House is the Kaʿbah.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r3.anchor: A valley without cultivation is a reference to Makkah (Kl), and Thy Sacred House is the Kaʿbah

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r4.claim: Prayer can stand for religion as a whole because of its superior rank, so the phrase means that they uphold religion; compare 42:13.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r4.anchor: Prayer here is said to denote “religion” in its entirety, in light of prayer’s superior rank in religion

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r5.claim: Though Makkah had no date trees, Abraham's prayer for fruits for Hagar and Ishmael was answered by produce brought from surrounding regions.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r5.anchor: Although Makkah did not have date trees, Abraham’s prayer to God to provide Hagar and Ishmael with fruits was answered

STUDYQURAN:14:37/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r6.claim: Some commentators say the prayer was answered through abundant date palms in nearby Ṭāʾif, which had substantial historical and commercial ties with Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:14:37/r6.anchor: According to some commentators, Abraham’s prayer was answered by the bestowal of abundant date palms upon the town of Ṭāʾif

TAB-FULL:v13p690/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts Abraham leaving Hajar and Ismail at Mecca by the House; Hajar trusted God's command, sought water, and ran between Ṣafā and Marwa as Zamzam emerged, after which Jurhum settled there and Abraham and Ismail built the House.
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " إن أول من سعى بين الصفا والمروة لأم إسماعيل، وإن أول ما أحدث نساء العرب جر الذيول لمن أم إسماعيل

TAB-FULL:v13p690/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r2.speaker: محمد
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r2.claim: The Prophet says that had Hajar not hurried to gather the Zamzam water, it would have remained a flowing spring.
TAB-FULL:v13p690/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «رحم الله أم إسماعيل لولا أنها عجلت لكانت زمزم عينا معينا»

TAB-FULL:v13p693/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r2.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's account Hajar makes seven trips between Ṣafā and Marwa, Zamzam wells up, Jurhum settles there, and Abraham later inspects Ismail's wives before building the House with him and calling people to pilgrimage.
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: " جاء نبي الله إبراهيم بإسماعيل وهاجر، فوضعهما بمكة في موضع زمزم

TAB-FULL:v13p693/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r3.speaker: محمد
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r3.claim: The Prophet says that if Hajar had left the water untouched, it would have been a spring flowing until the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يرحمها الله، لو تركتها لكانت عينا سائحة تجري إلى يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abraham settled Ismail and his mother in Mecca; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that this was when Ismail was first placed there.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع} [إبراهيم: 37] قال:

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r2.claim: The implied object after min is omitted: Abraham settled some of his offspring. Arabic often omits such an object because min already conveys partitive meaning, as in Qurʾān 7:50.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r2.anchor: فتأويل الكلام إذن: ربنا إني أسكنت بعض ولدي بواد غير ذي زرع

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r3.claim: The valley had no water then, Tabari argues, since a place with water would not be described as barren of cultivation.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r3.anchor: لأنه لو كان هنالك ماء لم يصفه بأنه غير ذي زرع

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r4.claim: To reconcile Abraham's settling Ismail before the reported later construction of the Kaaba, Tabari reports two prior explanations: the House existed before it was raised after the Flood, or God had already decreed it would be built there.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r4.anchor: منها أن معناه: عند بيتك المحرم الذي كان قبل أن ترفعه من الأرض حين رفعته أيام الطوفان

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r5.claim: Qatāda explains al-muḥarram as the sanctuary in which violating God's sacred limits and neglecting its due are forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r5.anchor: قاله قتادة معناه: المحرم من استحلال حرمات الله فيه،

TAB-FULL:v13p697/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r6.claim: In a sermon, ʿUmar says Ṭasm and then Jurhum violated the sanctuary and were destroyed; he warns Quraysh against doing likewise, noting prayer there is worth more than a hundred prayers elsewhere and sins there are similarly weighty.
TAB-FULL:v13p697/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: ذكر لنا، أن عمر بن الخطاب قال في خطبته: «إن هذا البيت أول من وليه أناس من طسم، فعصوا ربهم واستحلوا حرمته،

TAB-FULL:v13p699/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r1.claim: Abraham asks God to make some people's hearts yearn toward his descendants' dwelling, a prayer that they be granted pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r1.anchor: وذلك منه دعاء لهم بأن يرزقهم حج بيته الحرام،

TAB-FULL:v13p699/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says that had Abraham prayed for all people's hearts to incline there, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians would have made pilgrimage; the wording specifies some people, the Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37]

TAB-FULL:v13p699/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r3.claim: Mujāhid likewise says the partitive wording prevents the Persians and Romans from crowding the sanctuary as they would if all people's hearts were invoked.
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r3.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] قال: «لو كانت» أفئدة الناس «لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم،

TAB-FULL:v13p699/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r4.claim: ʿIkrima explains the phrase as people's hearts yearning toward the House and visiting it for pilgrimage.
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r4.anchor: سألت عكرمة عن هذه الآية: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] ، فقال: «قلوبهم تهوي إلى البيت»

TAB-FULL:v13p699/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r5.speaker: عطاء، وطاوس، وعكرمة
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs, and ʿIkrima gloss the people's yearning as pilgrimage and hearts drawn to Mecca to perform it.
TAB-FULL:v13p699/r5.anchor: عن عطاء، وطاوس، وعكرمة في قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] قال: «هواهم إلى مكة أن يحجوا»

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r1.claim: Ibrahim settled his descendants so they could perform the prayer obligations God imposed in the Sacred House.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r1.anchor: قال: سألت طاوسا، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي رباح، عن قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] ، فقالوا: «اجعل هواهم الحج»

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r2.claim: Ibrahim asked God to draw some people's hearts toward the dwellings of his descendants.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] قال: «إن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن سأل الله أن يجعل أناسا من الناس يهوون سكنى أو سكن مكة»

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r3.speaker: طاوس، عكرمة، عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r3.claim: They interpret the prayer as asking that people's longing for Abraham's descendants be for pilgrimage.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r3.anchor: قال: سألت طاوسا، وعكرمة، وعطاء بن أبي رباح، عن قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] ، فقالوا: «اجعل هواهم الحج»

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that asking for the hearts of all people would have brought Jews, Christians, and everyone to pilgrimage; Abraham asked for only some.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لو كان إبراهيم قال: «فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم» لحجه اليهود والنصارى والناس كلهم

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r5.claim: Qatadah glosses the hearts' inclination as being drawn toward them.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] قال: «تنزع إليهم»

TAB-FULL:v13p700/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Abraham asked God to make people desire living in Mecca.
TAB-FULL:v13p700/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم} [إبراهيم: 37] قال: «إن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن سأل الله أن يجعل أناسا من الناس يهوون سكنى أو سكن مكة»

TAB-FULL:v13p701/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r1.claim: God supplied them with plant and tree fruits like those available in settled regions with water and rivers, despite the valley's lack of cultivation or water.
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r1.anchor: وارزقهم من ثمرات النبات والأشجار ما رزقت سكان الأرياف والقرى التي هي ذوات المياه والأنهار

TAB-FULL:v13p701/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r2.speaker: محمد بن مسلم الطائفي
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r2.claim: A report says that when Abraham prayed for the Sanctuary's people to receive fruits (2:126), God moved al-Ta'if from Palestine.
TAB-FULL:v13p701/r2.anchor: قرأت على محمد بن مسلم الطائفي أن إبراهيم لما دعا للحرم: {وارزق أهله من الثمرات} [البقرة: 126] نقل الله الطائف من فلسطين

SULAMI:v1p348/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p348/r1.claim: Settling his descendants means placing them in God's presence by taking them beyond the bounds of known things and formal conventions.
SULAMI:v1p348/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أسكنتهم حضرتك بإخراجي إياهم عن حدود

SULAMI:v1p348/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348/r2.speaker: آخر
SULAMI:v1p348/r2.claim: Another says God eased their return to Him by allowing nothing in the two worlds to distract them from Him.
SULAMI:v1p348/r2.anchor: قال آخر : سهلت عليهم طريق الرجوع إليك ليلا بمجرهم

SULAMI:v1p348/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p348/r3.claim: Their dwelling in the barren valley taught them reliance on God and abandonment of reliance on material causes.
SULAMI:v1p348/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : علمتهم بذلك طريق التوكل وترك الاعتماد

SULAMI:v1p348/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p348/r4.claim: Ja'far explains that people's hearts incline toward Abraham's family because their own hearts incline toward God.
SULAMI:v1p348/r4.anchor: قال جعفر : لأن أفئدتهم تهوي إليك

SULAMI:v1p348/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p348/r5.claim: When someone withdraws completely from creation, God turns people's faces toward him and places affection for him in their hearts; Abraham prayed this for his family after cutting them off from people, provision, and causes.
SULAMI:v1p348/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من انقطع عن الخلق بالكلية صرف الله تعالى

TABATABAI:14:37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37/r3.claim: In “I settled some of my descendants,” min is partitive, while the phrase functions as the object of “settled” or stands in its place.
TABATABAI:14:37/r3.anchor: في تأويل مفعول " أسكنت " أو ساد مسده

TABATABAI:14:37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37/r4.claim: The descendants meant are Ishmael and the children to be born to him, not Ishmael alone, as the following plural purpose clause indicates.
TABATABAI:14:37/r4.anchor: ابنه إسماعيل ومن سيولد له من الأولاد دون اسماعيل وحده بدليل قوله بعد

TABATABAI:14:37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37/r5.claim: The Qur’anic account of Abraham’s earlier forgiveness prayer for his father says it was only because of a promise; when he learned the man was God’s enemy, he disavowed him.
TABATABAI:14:37/r5.anchor: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r1.claim: “Not of cultivation” means uncultivated in a stronger sense: rocky, sandy land lacking the materials needed for crops; he compares the wording with “a Qur’an without crookedness.”
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r1.anchor: غير المزروع وهو آكد وأبلغ لأنه يدل

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r2.claim: The House is attributed to God because it was built for a purpose belonging exclusively to Him: worship; its being sacred is a status God legislated.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r2.anchor: ونسبة البيت إلى الله سبحانه لأنه مبني لغرض لا يصلح إلا له تعالى وهو عبادته

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r3.claim: The phrase “at Your sacred House” syntactically modifies “I settled.”
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r3.anchor: والظرف أعني قوله { عند بيتك المحرم } متعلق بقوله

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r4.claim: The prayer’s mention of the House and settlement there shows Abraham made this supplication late in life, after building the Kaaba and populating Mecca; the verse about sons born in old age also supports this chronology.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r4.anchor: من الشاهد على ما قدمناه من أنه عليه السلام إنما دعا بهذا الدعاء في أواخر عمره بعد ما بنى الكعبة

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r5.claim: This timing removes the objection that Abraham called it a House before building it; proposals that he foresaw its future construction or that a prior House was destroyed or lifted away are unnecessary and fail to explain other wording on the same chronology.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى دفعه بأنه كان يعلم بما علمه الله أنه سيبني هناك بيتا لله أو بأن البيت كان قبل ذلك

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r6.claim: Abraham chose a barren, isolated valley without life’s comforts so his family would devote themselves to worship without worldly distractions.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r6.anchor: يفيد أنه عليه السلام إنما اختار واديا غير ذي زرع أعزل من أمتعة الحياة

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r7.claim: The hearts’ “falling” toward them means affection and inclination, through living near them or making pilgrimage to the House, so the family can find companionship.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r7.anchor: من الهوي بمعنى السقوط أي تحن وتميل إليهم بالمساكنة معهم أو بالحج إلى البيت

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r8.claim: God provides fruits by bringing them to the valley through trade.

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r6.claim: Reports that Taif was moved from Palestine to Mecca, circled the House seven times, then settled at its present site are possible as a miracle but weak and mursal, insufficient proof; such a great sign would have been mentioned in this passage of blessing.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r6.anchor: وهذا وإن كان ممكن الوقوع في نفسه من طريق الإعجاز لكن لا يكفي لثبوته أمثال هذه الروايات الضعيفة

AKHFASH:v2p409/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p409/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p409/r1.claim: من is partitive: Abraham settled some people from his descendants; بواد uses ب as Arabs say someone is in or at Basra.
AKHFASH:v2p409/r1.anchor: وكذلك قال {إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد} يقول: "أسكنت من ذريتي أناسا"

AKHFASH:v2p409/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p409/r2.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p409/r2.claim: Some explain تهوي إليهم as تهواهم, meaning that hearts love or long for them.
AKHFASH:v2p409/r2.anchor: وقال {تهوي إليهم} زعموا انه في التفسير "تهواهم"

TABRISI:14:37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وأبو جعفر الباقر وجعفر بن محمد ومجاهد
TABRISI:14:37/r2.claim: These authorities read تهوى with fatḥa on the wāw.
TABRISI:14:37/r2.anchor: وقرأ أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب ع وأبو جعفر الباقر ع وجعفر بن محمد ع ومجاهد تهوى إليهم بفتح الواو

TABRISI:14:37/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37/r10.claim: With fatḥa on the wāw, تهوى derives from loving something; إلى is licensed by the sense of leaning toward it.
TABRISI:14:37/r10.anchor: وأما قوله: { تهوى إليهم } بفتح الواو فهو من هويت الشيء أهواه إذا أحببته

TABRISI:14:37/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37/r11.claim: The construction is compared with 2:187: rafath takes إلى because it means making intimate approach.
TABRISI:14:37/r11.anchor: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم

TABRISI:14:37/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r12.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:14:37/r12.claim: Ibn Jinnī says the common reading means hearts incline toward and love Ibrahim's descendants; هويت فلانا and هوي إلى الشيء converge in meaning despite different forms.
TABRISI:14:37/r12.anchor: قال ابن جني المعنى في قراءة الجماعة تهوى إليهم تميل إليهم أي تحبهم

TABRISI:14:37/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r13.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:14:37/r13.claim: The phrase وهو ينحط في هواك means someone settles into and remains devoted to your inclination.
TABRISI:14:37/r13.anchor: وذلك أن الإنسان إذ أحب الشيء أكثر من ذكره وأقام عليه

TABRISI:14:37#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r5.claim: A wādī is a great mountain's slope; great rivers are also called valleys because their banks resemble mountains. Diyah denotes great property for a grave matter.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r5.anchor: الوادي سفح الجبل العظيم ومنها قيل للأنهار العظام أودية لأن حافاتها كالجبال لها

TABRISI:14:37#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r15.claim: Ibrahim settled some of his children there; the referent is Ishmael with his mother Hagar, and Ishmael was his eldest son.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r15.anchor: أي أسكنت بعض أولادي ولا خلاف أنه يريد إسماعيل ع مع أمه هاجر وهو أكبر ولده

TABRISI:14:37#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r16.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:14:37#2/r16.claim: Al-Bāqir says his family are the remnant of that lineage and Ibrahim's prayer was specifically for them.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r16.anchor: وروي عن الباقر ع أنه قال نحن بقية تلك العترة

TABRISI:14:37#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r17.claim: The barren valley is Mecca's al-Abṭaḥ; it then lacked water, crops, and livestock.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r17.anchor: يريد وادي مكة وهو الأبطح وإنما قال غير ذي زرع لأنه لم يكن بها يومئذ ماء ولا زرع ولا ضرع

TABRISI:14:37#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#3/r1.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:14:37#3/r1.claim: Al-Balkhī says أسكنت omits its object because min indicates part of a group; the estimate is people or a child, as in 7:50.
TABRISI:14:37#3/r1.anchor: وتقديره أسكنت من ذريتي أناسا أو ولدا عن البلخي

TABRISI:14:37#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#3/r2.claim: The House is attributed to God because He alone owns it, unlike other houses that can belong to servants.
TABRISI:14:37#3/r2.anchor: إنما أضاف البيت إليه سبحانه لأنه مالكه لا يملكه أحد سواه

TABRISI:14:37#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#3/r3.claim: It is called a House before Ibrahim built it because its future construction was known, or because it already existed and was destroyed by Ṭasm and Jadīs; another report says it was raised to heaven at the Flood.
TABRISI:14:37#3/r3.anchor: لما كان من المعلوم أنه يبنيه سماه بيتا والمراد عند بيتك الذي مضى في سابق علمك كونه

TABRISI:14:37#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#3/r4.claim: It is called sacred because access requires consecration; another view cites restrictions on sex and contact with impurity or blood, and a third means greatly honored.
TABRISI:14:37#3/r4.anchor: وإنما سماه المحرم لأنه لا يستطيع أحد الوصول إليه إلا بالإحرام

TABRISI:14:37-39/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r1.claim: Ibrahim settled them there so they would persist in prayer and establish it with proper conditions.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r1.anchor: أي أسكنتهم هذا الوادي ليداوموا على الصلاة ويقيموا بشرائطها

TABRISI:14:37-39/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r2.claim: The purpose lām connects to أسكنت; the vocative ربنا intervenes, a separation considered proper, as in the cited line to Zurayq.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r2.anchor: لأن الفصل بالنداء مستحب في هذا

TABRISI:14:37-39/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r3.claim: The line على حين ألهى الناس جل أمورهم فندلا زريق المال ندل الثعالب illustrates a vocative separating a verbal noun from its complement.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r3.anchor: على حين ألهى الناس جل أمورهم فندلا زريق المال ندل الثعالب

TABRISI:14:37-39/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r4.claim: Ibrahim asks that hearts yearn for the place, comforting his descendants through visiting delegations and providing ongoing provisions.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r4.anchor: هذا سؤال من إبراهيم ع أن يجعل الله قلوب الخلق تحن إلى ذلك الموضع

TABRISI:14:37-39/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r5.claim: Without God's kindness in drawing hearts there by pilgrimage, ʿumra, or trade, the inhabitants could not survive.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r5.anchor: ولولا لطفه سبحانه بإمالة قلوب الناس إليه إما للدين كالحج والعمرة

TABRISI:14:37-39/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:14:37-39/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says specifying some people avoided bringing Jews, Christians, and Magians to the sanctuary.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لو قال أفئدة الناس لحجت اليهود والنصارى والمجوس

TABRISI:14:37-39/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:14:37-39/r7.claim: Mujāhid reports that if Ibrahim had said all people's hearts, Persia and Rome would have crowded to the sanctuary.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r7.anchor: وروى مجاهد أنه قال: إن إبراهيم ع لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم

TABRISI:14:37-39/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r8.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:14:37-39/r8.claim: Al-Bāqir says people were told to circle these stones then come to the Imams to learn their loyalty and offer support; he recited this verse.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r8.anchor: وروى الفضل بن يسار وغيره عن الباقر ع أنه قال: إنما أمر الناس أن يطوفوا بهذه الأحجار

TABRISI:14:37-39/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:14:37-39/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda explain تهوى as being drawn or inclined toward them.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r9.anchor: وقيل إن معنى تهوي إليهم ينزع إليهم ويميل عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:14:37-39/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:14:37-39/r10.claim: Abū Muslim takes it as descending or landing, since Mecca lies in a depression.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r10.anchor: وقيل معناه وينزل ويهبط إليهم لأن مكة في غور عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:14:37-39/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r11.claim: The requested provision is so that they may thank and worship God.

FARRA:v2p78/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p78/r4.claim: The partitive من can stand without an explicit noun: “we struck some of Banū So-and-so”; compare the phrase about some water in 7:50.
FARRA:v2p78/r4.anchor: وهو جائز: أن تقول: قد أصبنا من بني فلان، وقتلنا من بني فلان وإن لم تقل: رجالا

FARRA:v2p78#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p78#2/r1.claim: تهوي إليهم means “want them,” as when a person يهوي نحوك, meaning he wants you.
FARRA:v2p78#2/r1.anchor: يقول: اجعل أفئدة من الناس تريدهم كقولك: رأيت فلانا يهوي نحوك أي يريدك.

FARRA:v2p78#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78#2/r2.speaker: بعض القراء
FARRA:v2p78#2/r2.claim: Some readers pronounce the verb with fatḥa on wāw, yielding “desire them”; compare ردف لكم for ردفكم and نقدت لها مائة for نقدتها.
FARRA:v2p78#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء (تهوي إليهم) بنصب الواو، بمعنى تهواهم كما قال (ردف لكم) يريد ردفكم

THALABI:v5p321#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p321#2/r1.claim: Min is partitive: Abraham settled one of his descendants, a son, in a barren valley at the Sacred House, namely Mecca.
THALABI:v5p321#2/r1.anchor: مجاز الآية أسكنت من ذريتي ولدا بواد غير ذي زرع وهو مكة

THALABI:v5p321#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p321#2/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the Sacred House as the sanctuary mosque, where God forbade disrespect and neglect of its due.
THALABI:v5p321#2/r2.anchor: قتادة: المحرم من المسجد محرم الله فيه، والاستخفاف بحقه

THALABI:v5p321#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321#2/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v5p321#2/r3.claim: One answer to how Abraham could say at Your Sacred House before building it is that the House existed at its site before the Flood, until it was raised from the earth.
THALABI:v5p321#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه عند بيتك المحرم الذي كان قبل أن يرفعه من الأرض حتى رفعته في أيام الطوفان

THALABI:v5p321#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321#2/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v5p321#2/r4.claim: Another answer is that Abraham meant the House that God had already decreed would be built in that land.
THALABI:v5p321#2/r4.anchor: وقيل عند بيتك المحرم الذي قد مضى في علمك أنه يحدث في هذا البلد

THALABI:v5p321#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p321#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p321#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas narrates that Abraham left Hajar and Ishmael at the House's site; when water ran out, Hajar searched between Safa and Marwa for help, and an angel opened Zamzam. The Prophet prayed for mercy on her, saying her haste kept it from flowing freely.
THALABI:v5p321#2/r5.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: إن أول من سعى بالصفا والمروة هاجر أم إسماعيل

THALABI:v5p322/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v5p322/r1.claim: In the story's continuation, the angel tells Hajar the spring will serve God's guests and Ishmael's father will return to build the House; Jurhum settles with her, and Abraham later visits.
THALABI:v5p322/r1.anchor: وقال لها الملك: لا تخافي الظمأ على أهل هذا البلد فإنما هي عين لشرب ضيفان الله

THALABI:v5p322/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p322/r2.claim: The story of Abraham, Hajar, and the station of Abraham had already been related in the commentary on Surat Al Imran.
THALABI:v5p322/r2.anchor: وذكر الحديث في صفة مقام إبراهيم وقد مضت هذه القصة في سورة آل عمران

THALABI:v5p322/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p322/r3.claim: The hearts are to rush or yearn toward Abraham's family; this is his prayer that they be granted pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
THALABI:v5p322/r3.anchor: فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي تفزع وقيل تشتاق إليهم وهذا دعاء منه (عليه السلام) لهم بأن يرزقهم

THALABI:v5p322/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v5p322/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says that specifying some people prevents Jews, Christians, and Magians from being included among pilgrims.
THALABI:v5p322/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لو يقال أفئدة الناس تهوى إليهم لحجت اليهود والنصارى والمجوس

THALABI:v5p322/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p322/r5.claim: Mujahid says the more general wording would have brought Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians to crowd the House; the verse specifies some people.
THALABI:v5p322/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

THALABI:v5p322/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p322/r6.claim: Abraham asks that his family receive fruits as people of water-rich villages do, so they may give thanks.
THALABI:v5p322/r6.anchor: وارزقهم من الثمرات ما رزقت سكان القرى ذوات المياه لعلهم يشكرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r1.claim: Al-Farra takes min as partitive: Ibrahim settled some of his descendants; Arabic can use min for a portion without stating the people affected, as in taking some food or water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: ولم يأت منهم بشىء (¬1) يقع عليه الفعل، وهو حائز أن يقول: قد أصبنا من بني فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r2.claim: Abu Bakr allows min to intensify the expression, with the sense I settled my descendants; he cites Dhu al-Rumma's use of min in poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر: ويجوز أن يقال: إن (من) دخلت لتوكيد الكلام، والتقدير: ربنا إني أسكنت ذريتي (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the descendants settled there as Ismail, one part of Ibrahim's progeny.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r3.anchor: قول ابن عباس في هذه الآية {إني أسكنت من ذريتي} يريد: إسماعيل (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the barren valley as the valley of Mecca; all of Mecca is a valley.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r4.anchor: {بواد غير ذي زرع} قال: يريد وادي مكة، ومكة كلها واد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r5.claim: Abu Ali prefers the first analysis and glosses it as settling people from among Ibrahim's descendants, with the object people omitted because the verb settle makes it understood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p487/r5.anchor: والقول الأول: اختيار أبي علي، قال: معناه إني أسكنت من ذريتي ناسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r1.claim: One explanation is that the Sacred House existed before being raised from the earth in the flood; Abraham settled Ismail in Mecca before they built it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r1.anchor: قيل معناه: عند بيتك المحرم الذي كان قبل أن ترفعه من الأرض حتى رفعته أيام الطوفان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the House was in God's prior knowledge as something that would arise in that valley.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r2.anchor: وقيل: عند بيتك المحرم الذي قد مضى في سابق علمك أنه يحدث في هذا الوادي (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses establishing prayer as worshiping God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد عن الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda, transmitting from al-Asmaʿi, says hawa means falling from a height to a lower place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r4.anchor: أبو عبيد عن الأصمعي قال: هوى يهوي هويا، إذا سقط من علو إلى سفل (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says an eagle hawat when it swoops down on prey or something else.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r6.claim: Al-Farra glosses tahwi ilayhim as desiring or heading toward them, like someone going toward you; the word can mean descending or coming down.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء في هذه الآية: {تهوي إليهم} تريدهم؛ كما تقول: رأيت فلانا يهوي نحوك (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r7.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's transmission, says hearts yearn to visit God's House; the yearning concerns pilgrimage, not the descendants themselves, and the prayer benefits believers and Mecca's residents through pilgrims.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r7.anchor: فأما قول المفسرين؛ فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد تحن (¬7) إليهم زيارة بيتك (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r8.claim: Qatada explains the hearts as being drawn toward them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {تهوي إليهم}: تنزع إليهم (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the prayer as asking that a group of people's hearts be drawn toward Ibrahim's descendants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r9.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي: اجعل أفئدة جماعة من الناس تنزع إليهم (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r10.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r10.claim: Mujahid says that if Ibrahim had asked for all people's hearts, Persia, Rome, the Turks, and India would crowd toward the place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r10.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد: لو قال: أفئدة الناس؛ لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says min limits the people to Muslims, since saying people's hearts without min would bring Jews, Christians, and Magians to pilgrimage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لو قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people whose hearts are meant are believers, both his descendants and others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p488/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في قوله: {أفئدة من الناس}: يريد من المؤمنين من ذريته ومن غير ذريته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi directs the reader to his explanation of this request in al-Baqara, at the parallel wording there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r1.anchor: ذكرنا تفسيره في سورة البقرة عند قوله: {وارزق أهله من الثمرات} [البقرة: 126]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p490/r2.claim: The purpose is that they might affirm God's oneness and exalt Him.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.claim: The account presents Abraham's grateful devotion and supplication as an example of servitude to God, and points to salvation through his monotheistic way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.anchor: Ayrıca Allah’ın verdiği sayısız ve sınırsız nimetlerin şükrünü yerine getiren bir kulun yani Hz. İbrâhim’in Allah’a karşı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r8.claim: After a sign from God, Abraham took Hagar and their son Ishmael to Mecca and settled them in a barren valley near the Kaaba, asking God to make it a settled, secure town.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r8.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim Allah’tan aldığı bir işaretle Hacer ve oğlu İsmâil’i Mekke’ye götürüp Kâbe yakınlarında tarıma elverişli olmayan, çorak bir vadiye yerleştirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r9.claim: The earlier prayer for the valley to become a settlement and a secure town is also related at 2:126.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r9.anchor: bu vadinin yerleşim merkezi ve güvenli bir belde haline gelmesi için Allah’a dua etti (Bakara 2/126)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.claim: Commentators say Abraham made the prayer in these verses after Mecca had become a settlement and he and Ishmael had built the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre İbrâhim bu âyetlerde bildirilen duasını da Mekke yerleşim merkezi haline geldikten ve İsmâil ile birlikte Kâbe’yi inşa ettikten sonra yapmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.claim: God answered Abraham's prayer by making Mecca secure and bringing produce grown elsewhere for worship such as pilgrimage and for trade; the commentary also directs readers to passages on Mecca and the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r11.anchor: Allah Hz. İbrâhim’in duasını kabul ederek Mekke’yi güvenli bir şehir haline getirmiş ve dünyanın muhtelif yerlerinde yetiştirilen ürünlerin gerek hac ve umre gibi ibadetler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r12.claim: The phrase translated “make people's hearts incline toward them” may instead mean “some people's hearts,” which would limit the request to believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r12.anchor: 37. âyetteki “İnsanların gönüllerini onlara meylettir” diye çevirdiğimiz cümle, “İnsanlardan bazılarının gönüllerini onlara meylettir” şeklinde de tercüme edilebilir.

BURHAN:v1p126/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.claim: Al-Baqara has baladan as the second object and āminan its adjective; Ibrahim has al-balad as first object and āminan as second, pointing back to the barren valley.
BURHAN:v1p126/r4.anchor: ﴿ بلدا ﴾ هنا هو المفعول الثانى و ﴿ آمنا ﴾ صفته

BURHAN:v4p416/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p416/r1.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p416/r1.claim: Al-Saffar says the preceding usage is not established in Arab speech; for that meaning Arabs use madh or mundhu, ending at the time of reporting.
BURHAN:v4p416/r1.anchor: قال الصفار وهذا الذي قاله غير محفوظ من كلامهم وإذا أرادت العرب هذا أنت فيه بمذ ومنذ

BURHAN:v4p416/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p416/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p416/r2.claim: Partitive min is indicated when it can be replaced by ba'd and the remainder still applies; Abraham settled some of his descendants in the valley.
BURHAN:v4p416/r2.anchor: الثالث التبعيض ولها علامتان إن يقع موقعها وأن يعم ما قبلها ما بعدها إذا حذفت

ITQAN:v4p330/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p330/r1.claim: The cited verses say the Book omits nothing and was sent as clarification of everything, grounding the claim that Qur'anic knowledge encompasses all matters.
ITQAN:v4p330/r1.anchor: ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

ITQAN:v4p330/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r2.speaker: النبي
ITQAN:v4p330/r2.claim: A report about coming trials says the way out is God's Book, containing accounts of the past, news of the future, and judgment between people; al-Tirmidhi and others transmitted it.

ITQAN:v4p330/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p330/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says the Qur'an contains knowledge for anyone seeking it; al-Bayhaqi explains that he means the foundations of knowledge.
ITQAN:v4p330/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال ( من أراد العلم فعليه بالقرآن

ITQAN:v4p330/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r4.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v4p330/r4.claim: Hasan says the sciences of the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were placed in the Qur'an after the sciences of all four scriptures were gathered into the Furqan.
ITQAN:v4p330/r4.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن الحسن قال أنزل الله مائة وأربعة كتب أودع علومها أربعة منها التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان

ITQAN:v4p330/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r5.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p330/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i says everything the community says explains the Sunnah, and the Sunnah in turn explains the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v4p330/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام الشافعي رضي الله عنه جميع ما تقوله الأمة شرح للسنة وجميع السنة شرح للقرآن

ITQAN:v4p330/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r6.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p330/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i also says that everything the Prophet judged was something he understood from the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v4p330/r6.anchor: وقال أيضا جميع ما حكم به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو مما فهمه من القرآن

ITQAN:v4p330/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p330/r7.claim: Al-Suyuti takes as support a report in al-Shafi'i's al-Umm that the Prophet permits only what God permits and forbids only what God forbids in His Book.
ITQAN:v4p330/r7.anchor: قلت ويؤيد هذا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p330/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v4p330/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says that every report from the Prophet he received in its proper form had confirmation in the Book of God.
ITQAN:v4p330/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ما بلغني حديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على وجهه إلا وجدت مصداقه في كتاب الله

ITQAN:v4p330/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p330/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says that whenever he narrated a hadith, he could point to its confirmation in God's Book.
ITQAN:v4p330/r9.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود إذا حدثتكم بحديث أنبأتكم بتصديقه من كتاب الله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p330/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r10.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p330/r10.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that every new religious case has guidance in the Book; even rulings first established by Sunnah derive from the Qur'an's command to follow the Messenger.
ITQAN:v4p330/r10.anchor: ليست تنزل بأحد في الدين نازلة إلا في كتاب الله الدليل على سبيل الهدى فيها فإن قيل من الأحكام ما ثبت ابتداء بالسنة قلنا ذلك مأخوذ من كتاب الله في الحقيقة

ITQAN:v4p330/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r11.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p330/r11.claim: Asked what a pilgrim in consecration should do if he kills a wasp, al-Shafi'i answered by citing the command to take what the Messenger gives; this illustrates deriving rulings through obedience to him.
ITQAN:v4p330/r11.anchor: وقال الشافعي مرة بمكة سلوني عما شئتم

ITQAN:v4p330/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p330/r12.speaker: النبي
ITQAN:v4p330/r12.claim: A report transmitted by Sufyan ibn Uyayna from Hudhayfa says the Prophet instructed Muslims to follow Abu Bakr and Umar after him.
ITQAN:v4p330/r12.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

ITQAN:v4p331/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p331/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ITQAN:v4p331/r1.claim: Sufyan reports from Tariq ibn Shihab that Umar ordered a pilgrim in consecration to kill the wasp.
ITQAN:v4p331/r1.anchor: وحدثنا سفيان عن مسعر بن كدام عن قيس بن مسلم عن طارق بن شهاب عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه أمر بقتل المحرم الزنبور

ITQAN:v4p331/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p331/r4.speaker: ابن برجان
ITQAN:v4p331/r4.claim: Ibn Barjan says everything the Prophet said, judged, or decided has a near or remote root in the Qur'an; readers grasp it according to their effort and understanding.
ITQAN:v4p331/r4.anchor: وقال ابن برجان ما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من شيء فهو في القرآن به أو فيه أصله قرب أو بعد فهمه من فهمه وعمه عنه من عمه

ITQAN:v4p331/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p331/r6.speaker: ابن الفضل المرسي
ITQAN:v4p331/r6.claim: Ibn al-Fadl al-Mursi says the Qur'an gathers the sciences of earlier and later peoples, fully known only to God and the one who spoke it, then inherited by the Prophet's most learned Companions.
ITQAN:v4p331/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الفضل المرسي في تفسيره جمع القرآن علوم الأولين والآخرين بحيث لم يحط بها علما حقيقة إلا المتكلم بها ثم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p331/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p331/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p331/r7.claim: Ibn al-Fadl recounts Ibn Masud's statement that if he lost a camel's nose-rope, he would find it in God's Book.
ITQAN:v4p331/r7.anchor: ثم ورث ذلك عنه معظم سادات الصحابة وأعلامهم مثل الخلفاء الأربعة وابن مسعود وابن عباس حتى قال لو ضاع لي عقال بعير لوجدته في كتاب الله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p331/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p331/r8.speaker: ابن الفضل المرسي
ITQAN:v4p331/r8.claim: Ibn al-Fadl says later scholars' energies and knowledge declined, so specialists divided Qur'anic studies into fields such as recitation, language, letter and verse counts, and structural divisions, often without interpreting or reflecting on its meanings.
ITQAN:v4p331/r8.anchor: ثم تقاصرت الهمم وفترت العزائم وتضاءل أهل العلم وضعفوا عن حمل ما حمله الصحابة والتابعون من علومه وسائر فنونه فنوعوا علومه

ITQAN:v2p518#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had Abraham asked for the hearts of all people, Jews and Christians would crowd to his descendants; specifying “some people” directs the prayer to believers.
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق السدي عن ابن عباس قال لو أن إبراهيم حين دعا قال فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لازدحمت عليه اليهود والنصارى

ITQAN:v2p518#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r2.claim: Mujahid similarly says that if Abraham had said “the hearts of people,” Romans and Persians would have crowded to them.
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن مجاهد قال لو قال إبراهيم فاجعل أفئدة الناس تهوي إليهم لزاحمتكم عليه الروم وفارس

ITQAN:v2p518#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r3.claim: Al-Suyuti takes these Companion and Successor explanations as explicit evidence that min in the prayer is partitive.
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r3.anchor: وهذا صريح في فهم الصحابة والتابعين التبعيض من من

ITQAN:v2p518#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r4.claim: One scholar observes that promises of forgiveness to believers omit min, while addresses to disbelievers use “from your sins”; al-Kashshaf says this distinguishes the two promises.
ITQAN:v2p518#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم حيث وقعت يغفر لكم في خطاب المؤمنين لم تذكر معها من كقوله في الأحزاب

BURHAN:v3p164/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p164/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p164/r3.claim: In Abraham’s prayer, “I settled some of my progeny,” an understood object is people or a group.

BURHAN:v4p233/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p233/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p233/r5.claim: A reading has تهوى إليهم with fatḥa on the wāw; alternatively, تهوى is understood to contain the sense of يميل.
BURHAN:v4p233/r5.anchor: بفتح الواو وقيل ضمن تهوى معنى تميل

ITQAN:v2p444/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p444/r7.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v2p444/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ilā as emphatic in a reading with fatḥa on the wāw, yielding tahwāhum; another scholar instead says the verb incorporates the meaning of tamīlu.
ITQAN:v2p444/r7.anchor: ومنها التوكيد وهي الزائدة نحو ﴿ فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم ﴾ في قراءة بعضهم بفتح الواو أي تهواهم قاله الفراء

DAMGHANI:v1p483/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r5.claim: Wādī can refer to Mecca, the valley where Abraham settled some of his descendants.
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r5.anchor: فوجه منها الوادي مكة قوله سبحانه في سورة إبراهيم رب إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r2.speaker: هشام بن عمار
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r2.claim: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār reads tahwī with an added yāʾ after the hamza, attributed to lengthening its kasra.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r2.anchor: وقراءة هشان بن عمار الدمشقي مقرئها الإمام، لآية إبراهيم: {فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً

NASHR:v2p299/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p299/r1.speaker: الحلواني عن هشام، والعباس بن الوليد عن أصحاب ابن عامر
NASHR:v2p299/r1.claim: Al-Ḥulwānī transmits from Hishām, and al-ʿAbbās from Ibn ʿĀmir’s companions, an extra yāʾ after the hamza in أفئدة here alone.
NASHR:v2p299/r1.anchor: فروى الحلواني عنه من جميع طرقه بياء بعد الهمزة هنا خاصة

NASHR:v2p299/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p299/r2.speaker: الحلواني
NASHR:v2p299/r2.claim: Al-Ḥulwānī says the yāʾ is either received non-analogically or reflects a familiar Arabic vowel-lengthening, as in الدراهيم والصياريف; Ibn Mālik attests elongation of all three vowels, and al-Farrāʾ cites أكلت لحما شاة.
NASHR:v2p299/r2.anchor: قال الحلواني عن هشام: هو من الوفود، فإن كان قد سمع فعلى غير قياس

NASHR:v2p299/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p299/r3.speaker: الحافظ الداني
NASHR:v2p299/r3.claim: Al-Dānī rejects the suggestion that a reporter merely mistook hamza easing for an added yāʾ; Ibn al-Jazarī likewise says this hamza is eased by transfer, not by that form of substitution.
NASHR:v2p299/r3.anchor: ورد ذلك الحافظ الداني، وقال: إن النقلة عن هشام كانوا أعلم بالقراءة ووجوهها

NASHR:v2p299/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p299/r4.speaker: الداجوني وسائر أصحاب هشام
NASHR:v2p299/r4.claim: The Dājūnī and most routes, along with the rest of Hishām’s transmitters, report أفئدة without yāʾ; the other readers also omit it.
NASHR:v2p299/r4.anchor: وروى الداجوني من أكثر الطرق عن أصحابه وسائر أصحاب هشام عنه بغير ياء
